4az1UIMaZI.one_liner: Fine-tunes transformers under task-agnostic patching to emit input-specific circuits for their own predictions as part of the output.
4az1UIMaZI.problem: Post-hoc circuit discovery is computationally demanding, faster approximations give less faithful circuits, and patching creates activations the model never sees in training, which distorts recovered circuits.
4az1UIMaZI.method: Self-supervised fine-tuning trains transformers under task-agnostic patching to produce input-specific circuits for their own predictions while preserving predictive performance; input-level circuits can be aggregated into a single circuit for a behavior.
4az1UIMaZI.key_idea: Make circuit discovery a training-time objective: the model learns to expose its own sufficient subgraph under patching, so patched passes are in-distribution.
4az1UIMaZI.evidence: Comparison of SDCM circuits with post-hoc methods such as EAP-IG across patching schemes and on a twin model that never saw SDCM training (per reviews).
4az1UIMaZI.claimed_gains: Discovers circuits far more efficiently than post-hoc methods, with substantially more faithful and concise circuits; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
4az1UIMaZI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results are strong and the self-discovering framing is new: one learned ranking beats per-scheme EAP-IG, including unseen patch schemes, and circuits transfer to a model never trained with SDCM.
4az1UIMaZI.main_concern: The faithfulness metric is the training objective (a KL), only sufficiency is tested, and missing ablations leave unclear whether gains come from fixing out-of-distribution patching or from reshaping the backbone.

qCLyaejIkB.one_liner: Self-supervised flow matching that concentrates noise on subject and decoy locations so relation conditions become necessary for reconstruction
qCLyaejIkB.problem: Self-Flow's random student mask does not target any semantic dependency and leaves most of the subject at the lower noise level, revealing its location without needing the relation condition.
qCLyaejIkB.method: Semantic Self-Flow places stronger noise where recovery depends on the semantic constraint; for spatial relations the subject is noised together with three alternative locations around the reference object, which stays at the lower noise level.
qCLyaejIkB.key_idea: Place noise by semantic dependency: noise the subject plus three decoy locations while keeping the reference object clean, so reconstruction requires the relation condition.
qCLyaejIkB.evidence: ImageNet experiments across model sizes with relation-flipped prompt evaluation and class-conditional FID, plus a leakage analysis and a human preference comparison against Self-Flow.
qCLyaejIkB.claimed_gains: When the relation is flipped under the same noise, both SSF outputs follow their respective relation conditions for 32% of test prompts, compared with 2% for Self-Flow, while class-conditional FID remains nearly unchanged.
qCLyaejIkB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem clearly defined and the decoy-plus-protected-reference design well motivated, with clear gains in relation following and little change to class-conditional quality.
qCLyaejIkB.main_concern: The ablations do not separate the effects of heavy subject noise, reference protection, decoys and mixed sampling, so the source of the improvement is unclear.

IlAkJHa45w.one_liner: Unifies text-to-image generation and editing: knowledge-enhanced planning, then editing-based self-reflective refinement, trained on a 300K reasoning dataset.
IlAkJHa45w.problem: Unified multimodal models struggle with synthesis tasks that need deep world-knowledge reasoning and treat generation and editing as isolated capabilities.
IlAkJHa45w.method: UniReason formulates generation as world knowledge-enhanced planning to inject implicit constraints, then uses editing for fine-grained visual refinement through self-reflection, in one shared representation. It is trained on a reasoning-centric dataset of about 300K samples over five knowledge domains plus an agent-generated visual self-correction corpus.
IlAkJHa45w.key_idea: Treat post-generation refinement as an editing step, so one model plans with world knowledge before generating and then edits its own output to fix errors.
IlAkJHa45w.evidence: WISE, KrisBench, UniREditBench, GenEval and ImgEdit benchmarks, with ablations of textual reasoning and visual refinement.
IlAkJHa45w.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract claims advanced performance on WISE and KrisBench while maintaining superior general synthesis on GenEval and ImgEdit.
IlAkJHa45w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that linking knowledge-grounded generation and editing as two stages of one reasoning process is useful, with ablations showing the full model beats reasoning-only and refinement-only variants.
IlAkJHa45w.main_concern: The method largely integrates existing techniques, and evidence for generation-editing synergy is insufficient because there is no matched-data comparison of joint versus separate training, with seeds and baseline protocols underspecified.

V84yBc0EgP.one_liner: FKCC weights each group-cluster distortion by the group's allocation to that cluster, building fairness into consensus clustering.
V84yBc0EgP.problem: Clustering ensembles must also account for how protected groups are distributed across consensus clusters, without enforcing profile alignment as a hard constraint.
V84yBc0EgP.method: Fair k-means Consensus Clustering (FKCC) lets the conditional proportion of a group in a cluster weight the distortion of that group-cluster cell, and center elimination gives an exact finite objective with monotone one-object descent.
V84yBc0EgP.key_idea: Weight each group-cluster cell's distortion by the group's conditional allocation proportion, giving quadratic assignment-dependent coefficients instead of separate fairness constraints or regularizers.
V84yBc0EgP.evidence: Theoretical analysis (allocation response, finite-empirical identity, uniform estimation under fixed-representation sampling) and experiments on nine datasets with matched KCC versus FKCC comparisons.
V84yBc0EgP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the allocation-dependent formulation is new and clearly motivated, avoids extra fairness regularizers, and is supported by strong theory and matched gains in clustering accuracy and group representation.
V84yBc0EgP.main_concern: The uniform-convergence guarantee assumes a fixed representation independent of the clustering sample, which does not match the experimental pipeline that builds ensemble representations from the same data.

0J8NnqyEpM.one_liner: Benchmark that holds the driving-scene image fixed and intervenes on text descriptions to measure MLLM reliance on textual cues.
0J8NnqyEpM.problem: It is unclear whether MLLMs for autonomous driving ground decisions in visual evidence or depend on the underlying LLM's parametric knowledge and textual context.
0J8NnqyEpM.method: TRUST-AD has 14,238 test cases across six safety-critical driving categories, systematically intervening on the textual prompt while keeping the visual scene fixed to measure decision stability, vulnerability to misleading cues and error recovery. An intervention-based attribution framework localizes failures to visual clues, traffic-rule information or both.
0J8NnqyEpM.key_idea: Keep the image fixed and intervene on the scene text, then attribute failures by testing whether visual clues, rule information, or both suffice for correct decisions.
0J8NnqyEpM.evidence: Evaluation of general-purpose and driving-specific MLLMs; reviews report 37 MLLMs from 17 families and 37 driving scenarios.
0J8NnqyEpM.claimed_gains: not stated (finds that conflicting text frequently changes decisions despite unchanged visual observations).
0J8NnqyEpM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is carefully designed and the large-scale evaluation and analysis are comprehensive and well presented, with interesting findings on accuracy versus robustness.
0J8NnqyEpM.main_concern: The vision-versus-text framing is not fully justified: correct decisions can legitimately need both, the protocol does not specify source precedence, and the benchmark mostly covers a static image plus traffic-rule text.

QumwilqkZy.one_liner: Adapts likelihood-free Bayesian optimization with tree-ensemble surrogates to maximize expensive set functions for feature, data, ensemble, and circuit selection.
QumwilqkZy.problem: Subset selection methods exploit modularity, submodularity, or low degree, but none of these hold exactly for any of the 321 set functions in the benchmark.
QumwilqkZy.method: The authors build certificates that quantify structural properties, find sparse, low-degree, hierarchical interactions in the set functions, and adapt likelihood-free Bayesian optimization (LFBO) to Boolean search spaces using tree-ensemble surrogates that learn improvement above a threshold.
QumwilqkZy.key_idea: Model the improvement above a threshold with tree-ensemble surrogates, which can represent the sparse, low-degree, hierarchical interactions found in these set functions.
QumwilqkZy.evidence: A benchmark of 321 set functions across four domains (feature selection, data selection, ensemble pruning, circuit discovery) under query and runtime budgets, against strong baselines including Gaussian-process BO.
QumwilqkZy.claimed_gains: The method ranks first in three of four domains at equal query budget and second in circuit discovery, where it matches the strongest Gaussian-process BO baseline at substantially lower computational cost.
QumwilqkZy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified formulation of four selection tasks and the structural analysis motivating tree surrogates are useful, and the evaluation across 321 objectives is extensive with strong baselines.
QumwilqkZy.main_concern: The advantage over GP-based BO and the contribution beyond LFBO are less clear than the headline ranking suggests, given time-based tie-breaking and extrapolated timings.

sj9rADnnRU.one_liner: First regret analysis of ReMax bandits, which sample from a distribution maximizing the expected maximum of M virtual posterior draws.
sj9rADnnRU.problem: ReMax, motivated by exploration under multiple attempts and related to pass@k objectives, had no regret guarantees in stochastic multi-armed bandits.
sj9rADnnRU.method: Given a posterior over arm values, ReMax picks a sampling distribution maximizing the posterior expected maximum arm value over M virtual draws; for Gaussian rewards they characterize optimal distributions via an expected-improvement balance condition and prove finite-time and asymptotic regret bounds.
sj9rADnnRU.key_idea: Decompose regret into a logarithmic term from rounds without optimal-arm underestimation and a dominant recovery term, using an expected-improvement balance condition.
sj9rADnnRU.evidence: Proofs for Gaussian K-armed bandits with any fixed integer M of at least 2, plus Gaussian-bandit experiments against Thompson sampling and KL-UCB.
sj9rADnnRU.claimed_gains: Finite-time expected regret O(sqrt((M-1)KT log T)) and an asymptotic logarithmic bound with coefficient at most M-1 times the Lai-Robbins optimum, which implies asymptotic optimality when M=2.
sj9rADnnRU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory is strong and elegant, linking a retry-based objective to sublinear and asymptotically optimal regret, and that the paper is well written.
sj9rADnnRU.main_concern: The theory assumes exact ReMax optimization and unit-variance Gaussian rewards while the main experiments use the approximate ReMaxGrad, and the finite-time bound hides a large gap dependence.

5f4catzyzC.one_liner: Conditions stochastic processes by pulling the likelihood back through a latent map and sampling latents with a guided reverse SDE
5f4catzyzC.problem: Stochastic processes are easy to simulate but hard to condition, because nonlinear observations, non-Gaussian likelihoods, black-box information, and global constraints induce intractable conditional laws that need bespoke constructions.
5f4catzyzC.method: LatentFlow writes the process as f0 = T_θ(ξ0) with ξ0 drawn from a simple reference distribution, pulls the likelihood back through T_θ, samples the resulting latent law with a tractable guided probability flow, and pushes the samples forward. Conditioning reduces to solving a single reverse-time SDE, with no learned neural approximations and no training.
5f4catzyzC.key_idea: Express the process as a deterministic map of a tractable latent innovation, so conditioning becomes latent-space inference solved by a guided reverse-time SDE with Monte Carlo drift estimates.
5f4catzyzC.evidence: Exactness at the level of the target law with explicit, bounded approximation errors, and experiments on Gaussian and heavy-tailed spatial processes, nonlinear stochastic dynamics, and mechanistic models, with wall-clock and ESS/s comparisons against NUTS and VI on 2-D toy targets per reviewers.
5f4catzyzC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is a unifying, training-free approach that applies to a wide range of stochastic processes under a mild latent-representation assumption, with correct theory.
5f4catzyzC.main_concern: Reviewers say the idea is an incremental extension of FlowGP and prior latent-space conditioning, and scalability and the accuracy of the score-correction estimate are not guaranteed.

Vxfxs3yJrv.one_liner: Searches model-merging coefficients on a small proxy model and transfers them directly to larger models in the same family
Vxfxs3yJrv.problem: Finding optimal merging coefficients needs an extensive search that becomes prohibitively expensive as model size and number grow, because of memory requirements and a combinatorially growing search space.
Vxfxs3yJrv.method: αTransfer optimizes merging coefficients on a small proxy model and transfers them directly to larger target models in the same family. Reviewers note it applies to evaluation-based and gradient-based merging methods with global, task-wise, and layer-wise coefficients.
Vxfxs3yJrv.key_idea: Models within a family show highly similar performance distributions over merging coefficients across sizes, so coefficients found on a small model transfer to larger ones.
Vxfxs3yJrv.evidence: Multiple merging methods, model families, and tasks, including vision transformers and large language models (a Qwen3-0.6B to Qwen3-4B transfer per reviewers), with ablations.
Vxfxs3yJrv.claimed_gains: A 6× speedup and 70% memory reduction on vision transformers, and a 20× speedup and 85% memory reduction on large language models, while maintaining comparable performance.
Vxfxs3yJrv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple, well motivated, and clearly presented, with experiments across merging methods and model families supporting coefficient transfer across sizes.
Vxfxs3yJrv.main_concern: Reviewers say the method needs fine-tuned checkpoints on the same data for both small and large models, transfer to newer merging methods is unproven, and one reviewer found unresolved numerical inconsistencies between language-model tables.

ZIF61XReMF.one_liner: An LLM agent runs the Bayesian optimization loop on a modular surrogate backend, using natural-language priors and revising strategy mid-run
ZIF61XReMF.problem: Existing LLM-based BO methods either fix the LLM into one role (surrogate, acquisition proxy, or configuration interface) or give it broad control that sacrifices systematic exploration, while richer domain priors are hard to encode through tailored kernels.
ZIF61XReMF.method: In agentic Bayesian optimization, an LLM agent (Sara) selects evaluations and can revise the strategy during the run by tightening bounds, proposing targeted evaluations, or reframing the problem. A modular BO backend (lenz) holds the probabilistic surrogate and exposes a structured interface the agent can inspect and modify.
ZIF61XReMF.key_idea: Keep the probabilistic surrogate in a classical BO backend that the agent calls as a tool, so the LLM supplies priors and policy control without acting as the surrogate.
ZIF61XReMF.evidence: Synthetic and real-world benchmarks (reviewers name LCBench, Yield, and one JAHS-Bench task) against standard BO and LLM-based baselines, with contamination controls such as shifted optima and renamed parameters, plus dynamic-setting experiments.
ZIF61XReMF.claimed_gains: Sara preserves the reliability of standard BO without prior knowledge, outperforms LLM-based baselines, and uses natural-language priors to improve beyond standard BO; no numbers stated.
ZIF61XReMF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that keeping the GP as a tool the agent calls is a useful combination of LLM reasoning and Bayesian optimization, beats LLM-only baselines, and is evaluated with careful handling of LLM contamination.
ZIF61XReMF.main_concern: Reviewers say the evaluation is thin and does not isolate what the agent adds beyond a well-configured GP (no backend-on-autopilot or LLM warm-start baselines), with selective benchmark choices and an unclear LLAMBO baseline implementation.

5zpTIz2Lly.one_liner: Generalizes SCORE's constant-curvature criterion to count data using concrete scores, giving conditional and off-diagonal curvature scores for DAG recovery
5zpTIz2Lly.problem: Score-matching causal discovery needs derivatives, which are unavailable for count data, and replacing them with finite differences does not generally suffice for causal discovery.
5zpTIz2Lly.method: The paper defines the conditional curvature score (CCS) for causal ordering by conditioning on the node's value, and the off-diagonal curvature score (OCS) for parent recovery, both built from score functions for continuous data and concrete scores for counts. The DISCO method estimates them with a diffusion-based concrete-score estimator per reviewers.
5zpTIz2Lly.key_idea: Condition SCORE's constant-curvature criterion on the node's value; zero CCS characterizes a semiparametric GLM whose conditional family need not be prespecified.
5zpTIz2Lly.evidence: Identifiability theory for bivariate and multivariate semiparametric GLM DAGs, plus broad experiments including a real-data check against seven domain-informed relations per reviewers.
5zpTIz2Lly.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the conditional curvature score is a simple, natural fix for count data, backed by exact identifiability characterizations and the practical advantage of not prespecifying a conditional family.
5zpTIz2Lly.main_concern: Reviewers say the consistency guarantee does not cover the implemented algorithm (diffusion-based estimation, standardization, boundary clipping), affine canonical parameters such as log-linear Poisson are not identifiable, and a closely related discrete-score method is not compared.

7X5bkYR9dA.one_liner: Predicts band-shared spatial operators with Gaussian supports instead of spectral values, enabling hyperspectral super-resolution across sensors and scales
7X5bkYR9dA.problem: Hyperspectral super-resolution models struggle to generalize across sensors with different band counts and to scales beyond the training range without extra data and computation.
7X5bkYR9dA.method: OmniHSR uses Cross-Spectral Mapping (CSM) to resample inputs with any number of bands to fixed reference positions and predict local operators with Gaussian supports. Continuous Operator-Field Reconstruction (COFR) then composes these operators into a continuous field applied to all original bands for arbitrary-scale reconstruction.
7X5bkYR9dA.key_idea: Predict one set of spatial operators shared across bands rather than spectral values, so the network does not depend on the input band count.
7X5bkYR9dA.evidence: Seven datasets with training on ARAD only and zero-shot transfer to six unseen sensors, twelve upsampling factors from ×2 to ×48, and comparisons with baselines trained from scratch or adapted on the target sensor.
7X5bkYR9dA.claimed_gains: Operator prediction outperforms direct spectral-value prediction on all seven datasets, OmniHSR (0.538M parameters, trained on ARAD) beats all directly transferred baselines on six unseen datasets, improves average PSNR on Pavia U and Chikusei by 0.55 dB over the strongest baseline, and runs up to 36× faster.
7X5bkYR9dA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that predicting band-shared spatial operators is an interesting design that decouples the network from band count and gives strong zero-shot cross-sensor results with a small, fast model.
7X5bkYR9dA.main_concern: Reviewers say the band-shared operator prior may fail for wavelength-dependent blur or band-specific detail, the evaluation uses synthetic bicubic degradation, and HSI-specific arbitrary-scale baselines are missing from the comparisons.

dkrS44C3mg.one_liner: Replaces softmax attention in spiking transformers with winner-take-all spike-driven attention for encoder and decoder language modeling.
dkrS44C3mg.problem: Spiking language models mostly rely on softmax self-attention, whose exponentiation and normalization raise computational cost and complicate neuromorphic deployment.
dkrS44C3mg.method: They introduce two softmax-free spike-driven attention modules, WTA Spiking Self-Attention (WSSA) and Causal WTA Spiking Self-Attention (CWSSA). They build an encoder-only WE-Spikingformer for masked language modeling and a decoder-only WD-Spikingformer for causal language modeling, both trained end-to-end.
dkrS44C3mg.key_idea: Winner-take-all selection yields one-hot (hard WTA) attention weights without exponentiation or normalization, so spike-driven attention needs no softmax.
dkrS44C3mg.evidence: Experiments on 16 datasets spanning natural language understanding, question answering, and commonsense reasoning, with a matched-architecture attention ablation against softmax and vision-based SSA, and operation-count energy estimates.
dkrS44C3mg.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only says experiments on 16 datasets validate the approach, with no numeric gains.
dkrS44C3mg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree vision-oriented spiking self-attention suits language poorly and WTA attention is a simple fix, coming close to softmax and well above SSA in the matched-architecture ablation.
dkrS44C3mg.main_concern: Energy claims rest on operation-count estimates rather than measured hardware and mix model sizes, and removing softmax does not remove the quadratic QK score computation.

jEj73nsoIa.one_liner: Flow matching that couples two independently corrupted views of one target in a single backbone, predicting both velocities jointly.
jEj73nsoIa.problem: Standard flow matching predicts velocity from a single noisy state, leaving the relationship between paths toward the same target implicit.
jEj73nsoIa.method: DualFM gives one backbone two independently corrupted states of a shared target and predicts both velocities in one evaluation. Independent training clocks vary the information in each view, while synchronized sampling evolves both states jointly; training stays simulation-free with no pretrained teacher.
jEj73nsoIa.key_idea: Train one backbone on two independently noised views with separate clocks, then sample both states on a synchronized clock so each informs the other.
jEj73nsoIa.evidence: Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet32, ImageNet64, and ImageNet256 (class-conditional pixel-space and latent-space SiT models), matched controls, and a proof that auxiliary conditioning weakly reduces irreducible regression risk.
jEj73nsoIa.claimed_gains: Improves multi-step generation over I-CFM with parameter increases of 0.104% for the RGB UNet and 0.257% for SiT-XL/4 and nearly unchanged large-batch sampling latency; FID values are not stated.
jEj73nsoIa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a simple modification with low overhead and consistent FID50K gains across settings, backed by parameter-, source-, and information-matched controls and ablations.
jEj73nsoIa.main_concern: Experimental coverage is limited (low-resolution generation, one seed on ImageNet64, no classifier-free-guidance results), and the theory does not guarantee that independent-clock training yields a good synchronized sampling field.

cpY9ygBWEB.one_liner: Junction-tree dynamic programming computes the characteristic-time sampling allocation for best-arm identification in factored multi-agent bandits.
cpY9ygBWEB.problem: In fixed-confidence best-arm identification for factored multi-agent bandits, computing the information-optimal sampling allocation is combinatorial because the joint-action space is exponentially large.
cpY9ygBWEB.method: The paper derives a junction-tree representation of the characteristic-time program in which locally consistent clique marginals characterize feasible allocations and a gap-augmented dynamic program handles competing joint actions without enumeration. It also introduces JT Track-and-Stop (JT-TaS), a delta-correct algorithm that asymptotically attains the instance-dependent lower bound.
cpY9ygBWEB.key_idea: Represent feasible sampling allocations by locally consistent junction-tree clique marginals and track cumulative reward gaps in a dynamic program, so complexity depends on induced width and gap-state width.
cpY9ygBWEB.evidence: Theory (exact pseudo-polynomial dynamic program for lattice-valued means, certified quantized approximation for real rewards, asymptotic optimality of JT-TaS) and experiments that recover the exact optimum on enumerable instances and scale to large joint action spaces.
cpY9ygBWEB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that identifying induced width and gap-state width as the controlling quantities is a clean, useful contribution that addresses a concrete computational bottleneck, validated against exhaustive optimization.
cpY9ygBWEB.main_concern: Empirical validation is thin: the full JT-TaS runs only on small enumerable instances, and the large-instance test exercises only the offline allocation solver.

ZZnPPrOTIA.one_liner: Trains masked diffusion LMs on reveal orders sampled from a teacher-extracted token dependency DAG, with no graph used at inference.
ZZnPPrOTIA.problem: Standard MDLMs weight all token reveal orders equally in training, whereas real generation lets some tokens be revealed concurrently while others should wait for prerequisite evidence.
ZZnPPrOTIA.method: MAPLE uses a frozen teacher (e.g., a pretrained LLM) to extract a dependency graph for each target sequence, which induces a normalized training distribution over reveal orders. It optimizes an exact negative ELBO that jointly models the next reveal position and token value, and uses the standard confidence-based decoder at inference.
ZZnPPrOTIA.key_idea: Extract per-sequence token prerequisite relations from a frozen teacher and use them to choose training reveal orders and supervise position selection.
ZZnPPrOTIA.evidence: Math, code, and text-to-SQL benchmarks across two model families and two corpora, with matched continued-training controls and comparisons to Efficient-DLM, TRIMS, and PUMA; theory shows global minimizers recover the data distribution under realizability.
ZZnPPrOTIA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree MAPLE provides relational supervision during training without adding any graph or module at inference, with strong math and code results across two model families.
ZZnPPrOTIA.main_concern: No ablation or control isolates the value of the prerequisite relations (for example random or simple-order graphs, or individual objective components), and the confidence-to-position mapping is under-specified.

bIkMmGA8Gm.one_liner: DirectMotion generates human motion directly in raw motion space with a lightweight DiT, removing feature and state redundancy.
bIkMmGA8Gm.problem: Latent-space motion generators need two-stage training and inherit autoencoder reconstruction errors, while raw-space generation suffers from feature and state redundancy.
bIkMmGA8Gm.method: DirectMotion combines a compact representation of root features and joint rotations, probability paths constrained to the state space of human motion, and clean-sequence prediction, with a lightweight DiT network.
bIkMmGA8Gm.key_idea: Remove feature redundancy with a compact root-plus-joint-rotation representation and state redundancy by constraining probability paths to valid motion states, then predict clean sequences directly.
bIkMmGA8Gm.evidence: Experiments on HumanML3D and SnapMoGen with ablations on removing each form of redundancy; reviewers cite a 9.2M-parameter model.
bIkMmGA8Gm.claimed_gains: Performs on par with larger latent-space models on HumanML3D and SnapMoGen; no numbers are given in the abstract.
bIkMmGA8Gm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and lightweight yet competitive on multiple datasets, and that the redundancy framing is informative.
bIkMmGA8Gm.main_concern: Novelty is limited because direct motion-space generation, rotation-manifold modeling, and clean-sample prediction were explored before, and the redundancy story is not fully validated.

4TdELAVM6d.one_liner: CalibHyper builds signed molecule-conditioned hyperedges from chance-corrected four-state label relations for few-shot molecular property prediction.
4TdELAVM6d.problem: Binary label agreement between assays is sensitive to class marginals and does not capture dependencies between properties.
4TdELAVM6d.method: An independence baseline is subtracted from the ordered four-state joint label distribution with shrinkage by joint observation count; a swap-equivariant relation head estimates residuals that define signed hyperedges conditioned on each molecule.
4TdELAVM6d.key_idea: Replace label agreement with chance-corrected residuals of the four-state joint label distribution, and use their signs to build molecule-conditioned signed hyperedges.
4TdELAVM6d.evidence: Thirteen molecular property datasets in 1-shot and 10-shot settings against many baselines, with ablations on chance correction, sign separation, routing, and auxiliary count.
4TdELAVM6d.claimed_gains: Competitive predictive performance on multiple molecular property prediction datasets; no numbers stated.
4TdELAVM6d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the chance-agreement problem under imbalanced labels is clearly diagnosed and the evaluation is broad.
4TdELAVM6d.main_concern: It is not shown that four-state relations and sign-separated coupling are necessary versus a simpler chance-corrected scalar relation.

y5DS1i7uTK.one_liner: Additive memory of transition embeddings for contextual MDPs, trained with STORE using random transition subsets and stored embeddings.
y5DS1i7uTK.problem: Optimal agents in contextual MDPs must update a posterior over an unobserved context at every transition, which is intractable, and Transformer or RNN memories are costly.
y5DS1i7uTK.method: MATE sums transition embeddings, exploiting the posterior's permutation invariance, which avoids growing Transformer rollout cost and recurrent backpropagation through time. STORE trains on a random subset of transitions per episode while reusing stored embeddings for the rest.
y5DS1i7uTK.key_idea: Accumulate transition embeddings additively, which is order-invariant and provably sufficient, so training can sample transition subsets and reuse cached embeddings.
y5DS1i7uTK.evidence: Diverse benchmarks (reviews mention Hopper, Walker and Cheetah-Vel) against sequence-model baselines such as GPT-2 and Mamba, plus theory on expressivity and gradient estimation.
y5DS1i7uTK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, well matched to the problem structure, efficient, and supported by theory and empirical results.
y5DS1i7uTK.main_concern: Ablations of the key STORE mechanism are insufficient, and timing protocols are not fully aligned (GPT-2 layer counts differ and some training times are estimated).

KQjPmwzhAr.one_liner: Batch regularizer that makes embeddings standard-Gaussian by enforcing uniformity on a sphere-interval product of direction and CDF-transformed radius.
KQjPmwzhAr.problem: Learning standard-Gaussian representations typically needs per-step Gaussian reference sampling, KL penalties or an inner transport solve.
KQjPmwzhAr.method: Embeddings are mapped to direction and CDF-transformed radius so Gaussianity becomes joint uniformity on a sphere-interval product, using a hyperspherical kernel and a reflected (Neumann) radial kernel whose excess energy equals a squared MMD to the Gaussian. A three-image pairwise approximation costs O(N^2 d), with an optional spectral approximation at O(NdK).
KQjPmwzhAr.key_idea: Express Gaussianity as uniformity on a sphere times an interval, with a reflected radial kernel making the product-uniform law the unique energy minimizer.
KQjPmwzhAr.evidence: Point-cloud tests, GPU memory and speed measurements at N=8192, d=128, K=16, and CIFAR-100 comparisons against SIGReg and analytic MMD.
KQjPmwzhAr.claimed_gains: At N=8192, d=128, K=16 the spectral repulsion uses 84 MiB instead of 2.6 GiB of GPU memory and is 3-14x faster than pairwise repulsion depending on the GPU.
KQjPmwzhAr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory clean, with a unique Gaussian target, an explicit counterexample for the spectral version's angular blind spot, and measured efficiency.
KQjPmwzhAr.main_concern: Better Gaussian matching does not clearly improve task performance (lower CIFAR-100 linear-probe accuracy than analytic MMD), and the construction overlaps with existing hyperspherical uniformity losses.

pk7AbXeMC8.one_liner: Distills RL specialists into a flow-matching VLA using critic-weighted action candidates, first on specialist-assisted then on on-policy observations.
pk7AbXeMC8.problem: VLA policies fail in short precision-critical phases, RL specialists that fix them leave auxiliary controllers and switching at deployment, and direct imitation of specialist rollouts reproduces jitter and misses the VLA's own states.
pk7AbXeMC8.method: At each critical-phase observation, REPAIR queries the specialist for several action candidates, weights them with its critic to form a supervision distribution, and trains the VLA with a shared weighted flow-matching objective first on specialist-assisted rollouts and then on its own rollouts; specialists are removed at deployment.
pk7AbXeMC8.key_idea: Weight multiple specialist action candidates by the specialist's critic to build a supervision distribution, trained on both specialist-assisted and student-visited states.
pk7AbXeMC8.evidence: Six real-robot tasks with 30 evaluation trials per task, plus ablations on action candidates, critic weighting and student-state supervision.
pk7AbXeMC8.claimed_gains: 100% success on all six real-robot tasks (30 trials each), with lower mean end-effector jerk than specialist-assisted execution on every task.
pk7AbXeMC8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the first-RL-then-distill idea is simple and timely, and that real-world results on long-horizon manipulation show strong success with smoother motion.
pk7AbXeMC8.main_concern: Reviewers say the closest prior distillation work (such as PLD) is not directly compared under matched budgets, the method depends on manually defined critical phases, and the writing is hard to follow.

V6UoWDZRxw.one_liner: Semi-supervised graph anomaly detection by discriminating known-normal nodes from the unlabeled population over normal-calibrated multi-hop representations.
V6UoWDZRxw.problem: Semi-supervised GAD with only verified normal nodes infers anomaly information indirectly, leaving unclear whether the unlabeled population gives direct supervision for anomaly ranking.
V6UoWDZRxw.method: KU-GAD builds normal-calibrated multi-hop graph responses and aggregates them with a hop-sequence Transformer, producing anomaly scores trained with a known-unlabeled discrimination objective.
V6UoWDZRxw.key_idea: Train a discriminator to separate known-normal nodes from unlabeled nodes, whose optimal score preserves the anomaly-to-normal likelihood-ratio ordering under a fixed representation.
V6UoWDZRxw.evidence: Seven graph anomaly detection benchmarks with ablation and sensitivity analyses on graph context, calibration and normal-reference quality, plus a population-level theoretical result.
V6UoWDZRxw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the known-unlabeled formulation gives a principled, clear population-level view of anomaly ranking, with strong performance and extensive ablations across seven benchmarks.
V6UoWDZRxw.main_concern: Reviewers say theoretical novelty is limited because it builds on density-ratio estimation, the KU objective's contribution is not separated from the architecture, and some baselines are copied from prior papers.

21u4Zq8BPu.one_liner: Rehearses proxy source data with reference-relative penalties to adapt Boltz-2 to macrocyclic peptide affinity without forgetting small molecules.
21u4Zq8BPu.problem: Adapting a molecular foundation model to macrocyclic peptides risks losing small-molecule accuracy, and retention must be estimated on a public proxy because the original affinity corpus is unreleased.
21u4Zq8BPu.method: Robust Proxy Rehearsal rehearses proxy data under penalties on each protein family's degradation relative to the pretrained model and adaptively emphasises families that degrade. A theorem shows the largest such degradation equals worst-case retention over family compositions.
21u4Zq8BPu.key_idea: Penalize each protein family's loss increase relative to the pretrained model rather than its absolute loss, and upweight families that degrade during adaptation.
21u4Zq8BPu.evidence: Instantiated with Boltz-2 over three random seeds and compared with uniform replay and other baselines on macrocycle and small-molecule affinity, plus a conditional bound separating sampling, within-family mismatch and missing coverage.
21u4Zq8BPu.claimed_gains: Improves on uniform replay on both sides of the trade-off, raising the median within-family Spearman correlation from 0.38 to 0.46 on small (the abstract is cut off there).
21u4Zq8BPu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem practical, the focus on degrading rather than highest-loss families sensible (Theorem 1), and the baselines and ablations extensive.
21u4Zq8BPu.main_concern: The reliability of the gains is unclear: configurations are trained once, hyperparameter studies show large variation, baseline tuning is uncertain, and worst-family retention is not tested directly.

1OpkOT3TFJ.one_liner: Scores video geometric consistency by measuring how each new observation increases an evolving world state's error on historical views.
1OpkOT3TFJ.problem: Existing geometric metrics compare frame pairs or model the whole sequence under one interpretation, so conflicts are hard to localize or anomalous observations get absorbed into the overall solution.
1OpkOT3TFJ.method: CAVE maintains an evolving world state and, at each timestep, queries identical historical views before and after the update, measuring the increase in historical explanation error. These responses form a geometric damage tensor used for video scoring, temporal conflict localization and spatial attribution, and the score also serves as DPO preference supervision.
1OpkOT3TFJ.key_idea: At each timestep, query the same historical views before and after assimilating the new frame and record the rise in explanation error as geometric damage.
1OpkOT3TFJ.evidence: Controlled geometric conflicts (reviews: 100 CO3D sequences with injected TPS warps), ablations, alternative observers (VGGT, TTT3R), and DPO post-training of a video generator.
1OpkOT3TFJ.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract gives no numbers; reviews cite 59% exact localization versus 27% for the strongest baseline under persistent conflicts).
1OpkOT3TFJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the observation-order, before-and-after-update formulation is meaningful, localizes when persistent conflicts enter a video, and gives a usable signal for DPO.
1OpkOT3TFJ.main_concern: Validation is limited to synthetic TPS warps of static CO3D scenes, with no correlation to human judgments or real generated-video failures, and scores depend on one frozen observer.

YEPCHTuvLa.one_liner: Calibrates conformal prediction under its own treatment-feedback shift via importance-weighted stagewise coverage and a self-consistent threshold schedule.
YEPCHTuvLa.problem: In sequential care, prediction sets influence treatment and change the outcome distribution, breaking exchangeability, so calibrating under the historical treatment process causes systematic coverage errors at deployment.
YEPCHTuvLa.method: SCCP formulates a self-consistent calibration problem, since the deployment distribution depends on the threshold being calibrated, shows stagewise coverage is identifiable from historical trajectories, and constructs a threshold schedule for the treatment process induced by its own use.
YEPCHTuvLa.key_idea: Estimate stagewise coverage under the treatment process induced by the threshold itself by importance-weighting historical trajectories, then solve for a self-consistent threshold schedule recursively.
YEPCHTuvLa.evidence: Asymptotic stagewise coverage proof; experiments on five benchmarks against Standard CP, ACI, MFCS and PRC, with ablations, feedback-strength sensitivity and calibration-size scaling.
YEPCHTuvLa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that performative feedback in conformal prediction for sequential care is an important problem and that prefix importance weighting with recursive threshold selection is a coherent solution, backed by broad experiments.
YEPCHTuvLa.main_concern: The guarantee is asymptotic and assumes accurate historical-policy weights, while experiments use simulated treatment mechanisms with a known policy, leaving estimation of an unknown logging policy untested.

rz5AvSazNN.one_liner: Jointly generates MOF building-block composition and all-atom periodic coordinates, with a diffusion process evolving every atom and the lattice.
rz5AvSazNN.problem: Useful generation of metal-organic frameworks requires building blocks that assemble into a periodic crystal with appropriate atomic conformations.
rz5AvSazNN.method: FlexMOF's coordinate diffusion incorporates chemical connectivity and dynamic periodic interactions while letting every atomic coordinate and the lattice evolve. Joint training uses structural supervision to shape the graph representation used for composition generation; at inference it first generates building-block graphs, then atomic coordinates and the cell conditioned on them.
rz5AvSazNN.key_idea: Train building-block graph generation jointly with all-atom coordinate-and-lattice diffusion so structural supervision shapes the graph representation, then generate coordinates conditioned on the generated graphs.
rz5AvSazNN.evidence: Boyd-Woo structure prediction benchmark, generation of valid, novel and unique MOF candidates, and pore-property evaluation, with topology and periodicity ablations (per reviews).
rz5AvSazNN.claimed_gains: Substantially better single-sample crystal structure recovery than the strongest reported all-atom baseline on the Boyd-Woo benchmark; the abstract gives no numbers.
rz5AvSazNN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it unifies structure prediction and de novo MOF generation with flexible building blocks and shows empirical gains over baselines across structure prediction, property evaluation and generation.
rz5AvSazNN.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the benefit of joint training or the periodic-image aggregation, whose formulation is close to Crystalformer, and some baseline comparisons use different sample populations.

zM7UJvW8dP.one_liner: Studies recursive retrieval-augmented forecasting with evolving memory, adding grounding to observed outcomes and reliability-aware adaptive memory updates.
zM7UJvW8dP.problem: Retrieval-augmented forecasters use static memory, but when previous forecasts are stored and reused, retrieval errors bias predictions, contaminate memory and reinforce later errors in a self-confirming loop.
zM7UJvW8dP.method: ECHO pairs predictive temporal retrieval with a fixed base forecaster and models memory evolution as a dynamical process. It analyzes when perturbations decay or amplify, introduces grounding that anchors memory evolution to observed outcomes, and adds a reliability-aware adaptive memory update.
zM7UJvW8dP.key_idea: Anchor an evolving prediction memory to observed outcomes (grounding) and adapt the memory update to retrieval reliability, to break the self-confirming retrieval loop.
zM7UJvW8dP.evidence: Experiments on four public benchmark datasets against a wide range of forecasting methods, plus a local stability analysis under a simplified scalar reliability model.
zM7UJvW8dP.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only competitive performance on four public benchmark datasets).
zM7UJvW8dP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that feedback loops from storing and reusing previous predictions in retrieval memory are a practically relevant problem, and the static versus recursively updated memory distinction is clear.
zM7UJvW8dP.main_concern: The self-confirming loop and stability claims are not directly demonstrated: the analysis uses a simplified scalar model, and memory evolves only on the validation split before being frozen for test evaluation.

WqFY4CKkSY.one_liner: Identifies joint potential-outcome distributions with cross-world factor models using J latent factors across K treatment levels.
WqFY4CKkSY.problem: Counterfactual queries depend on the joint distribution of potential outcomes across treatment levels, and identifying it needs a structural representation beyond the marginal outcome distributions.
WqFY4CKkSY.method: Cross-world factor models represent causal relationships across K treatment levels with J scalar latent factors. The paper characterizes when the representation is saturated (J at least K), derives identification of the joint potential-outcome distribution from conditional marginals under conditional mutual independence and loading-structure assumptions (J at most K), and develops a parametric maximum likelihood estimator.
WqFY4CKkSY.key_idea: Represent potential outcomes across K treatment levels through J latent factors that are conditionally mutually independent, so the joint law follows from conditional marginals when J equals K.
WqFY4CKkSY.evidence: Identification and saturation theorems, a parametric MLE, synthetic experiments, and a real-world randomized recommendation dataset from a short-video platform (per reviews).
WqFY4CKkSY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses an important identification problem in causal inference with a clearly formulated theoretical framework, supported by synthetic and real-world experiments.
WqFY4CKkSY.main_concern: Identification relies on hard-to-verify assumptions (independent latent factors, a manually specified factor-sharing structure, homogeneous loadings), and the comparison with existing counterfactual identification approaches is unclear.

u5hX9CEIuu.one_liner: Trains soft-robot loco-manipulation policies with analytic policy gradients through differentiable simulation, despite contact discontinuities.
u5hX9CEIuu.problem: Analytic policy gradients are widely considered impractical for contact-rich manipulation because contact discontinuities induce bias and stiff or chaotic dynamics yield high-variance, exploding gradients over long horizons.
u5hX9CEIuu.method: Soft robots with up to 2,420 actuated springs are trained end-to-end with first-order gradients through simulation and control, supported by gradient-energy analysis and per-layer rescaling of SGD.
u5hX9CEIuu.key_idea: Aggregate first-order gradients through differentiable simulation, and rescale SGD per layer so the wide actuation output layer receives its share of the sparse contact-mediated signal.
u5hX9CEIuu.evidence: Soccer-inspired single-agent, cooperative, and competitive multi-agent tasks on one commodity GPU, gradient-energy analysis, and optimizer comparisons over 20 seeds across three morphologies (per reviews).
u5hX9CEIuu.claimed_gains: A single agent learns to locate, pursue, dribble, and kick the ball through the goal in 100 gradient steps (under a minute on one GPU); a defender reduces opponents' scoring rate by up to 60%; per-layer rescaled SGD nearly matches Adam.
u5hX9CEIuu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the work shows analytic policy gradients succeed in a high-dimensional, contact-rich soft-robot setting, including multi-agent training, with convincing results and useful optimization tricks.
u5hX9CEIuu.main_concern: Comparisons are limited: no zero-order or short-horizon and critic-based first-order baselines such as SHAC in the same setting, and sensitivity to window length and contact parameters is unclear.

Uu1fbKxEAb.one_liner: Mechanistic analysis of how aligned diffusion language models redirect compliant-prefix attacks to benign content via sparse early-step attention heads.
Uu1fbKxEAb.problem: The safety mechanisms and robustness of diffusion language models under jailbreak attacks are poorly understood.
Uu1fbKxEAb.method: A systematic evaluation of DLMs and ARMs under a compliant-prefix attack identifies Benign-Shifted Compliance (BSC), where the model keeps the prefix's compliant surface form but redirects harmful intent to benign content. Mechanistic analysis and targeted activation steering of attention heads probe the earliest denoising steps.
Uu1fbKxEAb.key_idea: Safety representations and refusal trajectories diverge in the earliest denoising steps, mediated by a sparse set of attention heads whose causal disruption bypasses the benign redirection.
Uu1fbKxEAb.evidence: Evaluation across model families and sizes of DLMs and ARMs under a compliant-prefix attack (plus Context Nesting per reviews), with head probing and activation-steering interventions.
Uu1fbKxEAb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a distinctive DLM safety behavior and connects early denoising dynamics, sparse head-level signals, and activation steering into a coherent causal story.
Uu1fbKxEAb.main_concern: BSC is loosely coupled to the later head-probing and steering experiments, and the scope (prefix attacks only) and novelty over prior work on early decoding steps and ARM steering risk overclaiming.

Suu0nVNNeZ.one_liner: Benchmark of RNA molecular dynamics trajectories plus a unified model for trajectory generation and dynamics fingerprint extraction.
Suu0nVNNeZ.problem: Large-scale standardized RNA dynamics data are limited, and existing approaches treat trajectory generation and dynamics understanding as separate objectives.
Suu0nVNNeZ.method: RNADynBench has 2585 quality-controlled 100-ns all-atom MD trajectories with leakage-controlled splits. RNADynNet uses a shared backbone with coordinate denoising, single-frame-to-trajectory alignment, and physical grounding to generate trajectories and extract dynamics fingerprints from a single conformer.
Suu0nVNNeZ.key_idea: Share one backbone between all-atom trajectory generation and single-conformer dynamics fingerprinting, tying them together with alignment and physical-grounding objectives.
Suu0nVNNeZ.evidence: Two test sets including a high-flexibility challenge set, with baselines adapted from protein work (per reviews) and ablations of alignment and physical grounding.
Suu0nVNNeZ.claimed_gains: Generated trajectories achieve RMSF correlations of 0.875 and 0.766 across the two test sets, with single-conformer predictions showing comparable agreement with MD-derived dynamics.
Suu0nVNNeZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dataset is a valuable, larger-than-existing RNA MD resource and the model shows good results over comprehensive metrics and baselines.
Suu0nVNNeZ.main_concern: The generation metrics (geometry, RMSF correlation, PCA-W2) are ensemble-level and do not establish temporal fidelity, so it is unclear the resource works as a benchmark of dynamics.

wZ1H37pwNV.one_liner: Factorizes interactions into ordered Request, Item, Context, Action states in one causal sequence; retrieval and ranking read different states.
wZ1H37pwNV.problem: Cascaded recommenders use the same user history for retrieval and ranking, although the two stages have different information available at different points of an interaction.
wZ1H37pwNV.method: LIFT models each interaction as an ordered Request, Item, Context, Action causal sequence with Role-Conditioned Attention and a lightweight Pre-LN Bias. Retrieval reads the Request state and ranking reads the Context state, sharing history modeling.
wZ1H37pwNV.key_idea: Place Request, Item, Context, and Action states in a shared causal sequence and read retrieval from the Request state and ranking from the Context state.
wZ1H37pwNV.evidence: ML-20M and Taobao against joint-model baselines, with loss-weight sweeps, sequence-layout and component ablations, scaling analyses, and three seeds (per reviews).
wZ1H37pwNV.claimed_gains: Highest Joint Score among evaluated joint models on ML-20M and Taobao, improving over the strongest baselines by 4.9% and 3.6%, respectively.
wZ1H37pwNV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is clear and the lifecycle factorization with stage-aligned readouts is principled, with consistent gains and targeted ablations.
wZ1H37pwNV.main_concern: Evaluation uses separate retrieval and ranking metrics on public logs without final reranked-list quality, and the gain may come from access to request-time features rather than the architecture.

CuI49ixOax.one_liner: MOF-conditioned normalized proposal over CO2 position, orientation, and deformation enables importance-weighted Henry coefficient estimation without per-material retraining.
CuI49ixOax.problem: Conventional Widom insertion spends many MLIP energy evaluations on unfavorable configurations, limiting the scale of MOF screening for CO2 adsorption in direct air capture.
CuI49ixOax.method: Equivariant MOF features from a pretrained MLIP, computed once and reused across draws, parameterize periodically wrapped Gaussian position mixtures and conditional orientation and deformation mixtures. This gives a normalized proposal with direct sampling and density evaluation for importance-weighted estimation with flexible molecules.
CuI49ixOax.key_idea: Condition a closed-form mixture proposal over CO2 pose and deformation on pretrained MLIP equivariant MOF features, so one transferable model supplies importance weights for unseen MOFs.
CuI49ixOax.evidence: Unseen MOFs spanning weak to strong adsorption (hundreds of held-out MOFs split by adsorption-strength quartile, per reviews), comparing sampling efficiency and reweighted configuration and energy distributions with reference methods, flexible-gas AIS, and rigid-gas Widom insertion.
CuI49ixOax.claimed_gains: Estimates flexible- and rigid-gas Henry coefficients at roughly 1,780- and 3,810-fold lower inference cost than flexible-gas AIS and rigid-gas Widom insertion, respectively, while maintaining high sampling efficiency.
CuI49ixOax.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the probabilistic formulation is technically careful (periodicity, coordinate Jacobians, oxygen-exchange symmetry), with good computational results on held-out MOFs.
CuI49ixOax.main_concern: Transferability is shown only within a filtered structural distribution split by MOF identifier, and novelty is limited since the method integrates established tools without isolating its key design choice.

ZV01BTYSjh.one_liner: Specifies Gaussian coordinate and simplex atom-type forward paths directly, with Concrete-sample observations and a GeoRank slot prior, for SBDD diffusion.
ZV01BTYSjh.problem: Recent Bayesian and flow-based generators have challenged diffusion in structure-based drug design, so diffusion's forward trajectories and intermediate atom-type representations need re-examination.
ZV01BTYSjh.method: MEGA specifies Gaussian coordinate marginals and categorical parameter trajectories on the simplex, and feeds the network stochastic Concrete samples of atom-type parameters instead of hard one-hot observations. GeoRank adds a geometric prior giving persistent slot identities without reference ligand conformations at inference.
ZV01BTYSjh.key_idea: Directly specify forward marginals (Gaussian for coordinates, simplex trajectories for atom types) and give the network Concrete-sampled graded atom-type evidence rather than one-hot observations.
ZV01BTYSjh.evidence: Benchmarks against compared methods on CrossDocked2020, with appendix ablations on the forward schedule, continuous atom-type observations, and GeoRank variants.
ZV01BTYSjh.claimed_gains: Leads the compared methods in 12 of 15 reported benchmark statistics, including all Vina evaluations, PoseBusters validity and strain energy, with 89.5% PoseBusters validity and a mean Vina score of -6.96 kcal/mol.
ZV01BTYSjh.reviewer_consensus: All three reviewers credit the competitive CrossDocked2020 results (Vina, PoseBusters validity, strain energy) and a well-motivated redesign of forward paths and atom-type observations.
ZV01BTYSjh.main_concern: Limited methodological novelty, since Gaussian marginal-first diffusion, simplex interpolation and Concrete sampling are existing techniques, and GeoRank's independent contribution is weakly validated.

pNvWEzULhc.one_liner: Two-stage cross-domain compositing: signed style-content graph learning disentangles style and content, then style-gap-aware modulation conditions a DiT.
pNvWEzULhc.problem: Cross-domain image compositing must preserve foreground identity while stylizing it to the background domain, but existing training-free approaches only reach tone-level alignment and lack large-scale paired training data.
pNvWEzULhc.method: They build ChameleonDataset with an evaluation benchmark through a scalable pipeline, then train ChameleonEncoder with Signed Style-Content Graph Learning (SSCGL) and inject its tokens into a DiT with style-gap-aware modulation (SGAM).
pNvWEzULhc.key_idea: Train an encoder with signed style-content graph learning to separate style from content, then modulate DiT injection according to the style gap between foreground and background.
pNvWEzULhc.evidence: Evaluation on the new ChameleonDataset benchmark, with a VLM-based scoring rubric and a user study as described in the reviews.
pNvWEzULhc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the reverse data pipeline that uses real images as ground-truth composites, the value of ChameleonDataset, and clear writing with fairly comprehensive experiments.
pNvWEzULhc.main_concern: Evaluation and data filtering rely on VLM judgments (rubric, keep scores) that are not validated against human judgment, and benchmark separation from training data is unclear.

Z4Ib1YaBTU.one_liner: Shows coupling destabilizes underdamped Langevin minimax dynamics, and an anchored scheme freezing strategies between Gibbs-response runs restores last-iterate convergence.
Z4Ib1YaBTU.problem: Underdamped Langevin methods are attractive in mean-field optimization, but their stability when two distributional players are coupled in minimax problems is unclear.
Z4Ib1YaBTU.method: For a bilinear game they derive an exact friction-coupling threshold separating stable and unstable underdamped dynamics, while the overdamped counterpart stays stable at every coupling. They then propose an anchored scheme that freezes current strategies, runs underdamped Langevin toward their Gibbs responses, and updates strategies between runs, plus a finite-particle discrete-time implementation.
Z4Ib1YaBTU.key_idea: Freeze both players' strategies while underdamped Langevin runs toward each Gibbs response, then update strategies between runs, avoiding simultaneous cross-player coupling.
Z4Ib1YaBTU.evidence: Theory: an exact stability threshold for a bilinear game, instability for a bounded smooth interaction, last-iterate convergence for convex-concave mean-field functionals, and a finite-particle guarantee; reviewers describe the numerical experiments as limited.
Z4Ib1YaBTU.claimed_gains: Last-iterate convergence with an O(1/K) decay of the Nikaido-Isoda error for convex-concave functionals of probability laws in the mean-field setting.
Z4Ib1YaBTU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question meaningful and the theoretical results relatively complete, non-trivial and clearly presented, especially the contrast between underdamped instability and overdamped stability.
Z4Ib1YaBTU.main_concern: Novelty is unclear because the algorithm appears to combine existing anchored best-response and underdamped Langevin work, and the numerical evaluation is limited.

114VH5fBSr.one_liner: Evaluates on-device LLMs by timely accuracy and request energy, and selects the lowest-energy configuration meeting deadline and accuracy targets.
114VH5fBSr.problem: On-device LLM systems are optimized for token throughput or energy per token, which do not show whether a request is answered correctly and on time.
114VH5fBSr.method: PACE measures timely accuracy (fraction of requests answered correctly before a deadline) and total request energy across deployment path, execution mode and generation budget. PACE-SELECT is a calibration-based rule that picks the lowest-energy configuration satisfying a target timely accuracy.
114VH5fBSr.key_idea: Compare configurations by energy per timely correct answer and choose the lowest-energy one that meets a target timely accuracy on calibration data.
114VH5fBSr.evidence: Qwen2.5-3B across three deployment paths on OnePlus Ace 6 and Redmi K90 phones, BitNet-2B and Llama 3.1-8B comparisons on QNN, and unseen requests on a OnePlus Ace7 Pro and HammerBench function calling, with external power-meter measurements per the reviews.
114VH5fBSr.claimed_gains: Two deployments with only a 1.01% difference in energy per token differ by 2.14x in energy per timely correct answer at a 10-second deadline.
114VH5fBSr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the careful measurement design (external power meter, repeats, paired requests, byte-identical outputs) and the clear motivation and presentation.
114VH5fBSr.main_concern: The value of timely accuracy and the deadlines are not tied to real applications, the selection rule is simple with limited novelty, and calibration and evaluation reuse the same request pool.

zdVeuoKRVN.one_liner: Away-step Frank-Wolfe updates with one LMO call per set give fully projection-free minimax methods over polytopes with improved complexities.
zdVeuoKRVN.problem: Existing fully projection-free methods for constrained minimax problems have much worse iteration complexities than projection-based counterparts.
zdVeuoKRVN.method: A fully projection-free method for polytope-constrained minimax problems that uses away-step Frank-Wolfe updates to exploit polyhedral geometry, needing one linear minimization oracle call over each feasible set per iteration.
zdVeuoKRVN.key_idea: Use away-step Frank-Wolfe updates on both players to exploit polyhedral geometry, with a single LMO call per feasible set per iteration.
zdVeuoKRVN.evidence: Convergence analysis for nonconvex-concave, one-sided Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz, convex-nonconcave and convex-concave problems, plus numerical experiments on two relatively simple problems per the reviews.
zdVeuoKRVN.claimed_gains: Nonconvex-concave complexity improves from O(eps^-6) to O(eps^-3), one-sided KL gives O(eps^-max{2,4 theta}), and single-loop convex-concave complexity improves from O(eps^-5) to O(eps^-2).
zdVeuoKRVN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives non-trivial convergence rate improvements across several minimax settings and is well written.
zdVeuoKRVN.main_concern: The experiments cover only two simple problems that cheaper projection-based methods could handle, which weakens the practical motivation.

8hdbsagylT.one_liner: Dynamic scale-weighted multiscale fusion guides selection among experts of different hidden widths for histology-guided spatial transcriptomics super-resolution.
8hdbsagylT.problem: Histology-guided super-resolution of spot-aggregated spatial transcriptomics uses fixed context combinations or uniform-capacity prediction branches, limiting adaptation to local tissue and molecular information.
8hdbsagylT.method: DAST builds multiscale contexts after pathology feature encoding, interacts each scale with local expression features, and learns scale contributions dynamically. The fused content and scale weights then guide selection among experts with different hidden widths to predict superpixel-level gene expression under spot-aggregated supervision.
8hdbsagylT.key_idea: Learn scale weights from multimodal features and use the fused content plus weights to route among experts of different hidden widths.
8hdbsagylT.evidence: Ten Visium HD and Xenium datasets against six other methods, with factorial comparisons, ablations, and downstream analyses of spatial domain identification and TLS-associated expression.
8hdbsagylT.claimed_gains: Lowest RMSE and highest SSIM compared with six other methods across ten Visium HD and Xenium datasets.
8hdbsagylT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results are consistently better across many datasets and two platforms, and find the adaptive multiscale fusion sensible with ablations supporting the design.
8hdbsagylT.main_concern: Table 1 lacks error bars and baseline fairness is unclear, while novelty over HISTEX is modest and the evaluation uses computationally aggregated spots that may not reflect real platform characteristics.

5RnAhz1Hfh.one_liner: Evolutionary search with a response-discriminating reward and a learned conditional mutation operator generates transcriptome-conditioned molecules.
5RnAhz1Hfh.problem: Transcriptome-based drug design generators struggle to achieve both high structural similarity to known actives and scaffold novelty, and their outputs do not guide subsequent proposals.
5RnAhz1Hfh.method: GxEvo is a population-based evolutionary framework with a condition-specific seed generator, a forward response model trained with response prediction and contrastive learning to discriminate candidates, and a learned mutation operator conditioned on the parent molecule and target condition.
5RnAhz1Hfh.key_idea: Use a contrastively trained forward response model as fitness and a mutation operator conditioned on parent and target condition so evaluated candidates steer later proposals.
5RnAhz1Hfh.evidence: Ten gene-knockdown targets and three held-out drug-cell splits, with matched candidate-budget controls on knockdown targets, random ZINC and ChEMBL molecule controls, and an external response predictor in the appendix per the reviews.
5RnAhz1Hfh.claimed_gains: Highest mean structural similarity to reference compounds among evaluated methods, and 23.8 structurally hit-like unseen scaffolds per 100 valid molecules on knockdown targets versus 3.9 for the strongest prior method.
5RnAhz1Hfh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the population-level evaluation, the extensive controls and baselines (budget-matched resampling, random molecules), and the reasonable refinement-based approach.
5RnAhz1Hfh.main_concern: Evaluation relies on proxies (structural similarity and predicted transcriptional responses) without experimental validation, and held-out comparisons do not match search budgets.

cRkzYG2qiM.one_liner: Casts classifier-free guidance as optimal control and constrains the control set to a hypersphere, giving curvature-aware guidance.
cRkzYG2qiM.problem: CFG degrades image quality and diversity at high guidance strength and violates principled diffusion sampling dynamics, while existing explanations disagree or do not extend to deterministic samplers.
cRkzYG2qiM.method: They frame CFG sampling as continuous-time optimal control and solve the HJB equation, recovering CFG under specific path costs with an unconstrained control set. CACFG then constrains the control set to a hypersphere informed by the Gaussian regularisation used in VAE training.
cRkzYG2qiM.key_idea: Constrain the guidance control to a hypersphere informed by VAE Gaussian regularisation, implemented as one norm and one rescale per sampling step.
cRkzYG2qiM.evidence: An HJB derivation that unifies CFG, CFG++ and IntCFG, plus image-generation experiments comparing guidance methods, with FID reported across guidance scales per the reviews.
cRkzYG2qiM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the unifying optimal-control view that expresses CFG, CFG++ and IntCFG as one family differing in cost scale, together with clear writing and a simple, low-overhead method.
cRkzYG2qiM.main_concern: The derivation works backwards from CFG and so explains little, and the claimed failure mechanism is not validated because FID still rises with guidance scale under CACFG.

1aQ0OuhtdV.one_liner: Generates each weight matrix on demand from compressed latent codes via small learned decoders, storing fewer parameters and optimizer states.
1aQ0OuhtdV.problem: Quantization lowers precision but leaves the number of trainable parameters unchanged, so gradients and optimizer states still dominate training memory.
1aQ0OuhtdV.method: Latent Tensor Rematerialization (LTR) generates each weight matrix on demand from compressed latent codes with small learned generators, turning a matrix into a recomputable activation. Bicameral is a LLaMA-style transformer whose weight matrices are generated by small decoders.
1aQ0OuhtdV.key_idea: Replace stored weight matrices with small learned decoders that regenerate them from latent codes at compute time, trading spare compute for fewer stored parameters and optimizer states.
1aQ0OuhtdV.evidence: Bicameral models with 2B effective parameters trained to 10B tokens, evaluated on perplexity and six zero-shot downstream tasks, plus memory and latency measurements with custom kernels per the reviews.
1aQ0OuhtdV.claimed_gains: Bicameral models with 2B effective parameters trained to 10B tokens match the uncompressed baseline on perplexity and zero-shot benchmarks (the abstract's memory-reduction figures are truncated).
1aQ0OuhtdV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cutting stored parameters, gradients and optimizer states is a well-motivated goal and that the half-storage model nearly matches a standard 2B model, backed by real memory and latency measurements.
1aQ0OuhtdV.main_concern: Evidence is a single 2B configuration trained for only 10B tokens with one run, with no comparison to other memory-efficient pretraining baselines such as GaLore and no distributed-training measurements.

beuggvXtxi.one_liner: Encodes LLM-generated hypotheses as conditional Gaussian process experts, scoring them by predictive feedback to evolve hypotheses and guide Bayesian optimization.
beuggvXtxi.problem: LLMs can propose domain hypotheses for Bayesian optimization, but assessing their reliability, turning them into numerical guidance and revising them as evidence accumulates remains hard.
beuggvXtxi.method: LLM hypotheses are encoded as conditional GP models that quantify their numerical effects, and prospective forecast evaluation updates hypothesis credits that govern acquisition and hypothesis selection. At scheduled interventions the LLM revises, recombines and proposes hypotheses using the observations and credits.
beuggvXtxi.key_idea: Score each LLM hypothesis, held as a conditional GP expert, by prospective forecast accuracy, and use the credits both to weight acquisition and to drive LLM revision.
beuggvXtxi.evidence: Four offline scientific optimization tasks spanning analytical chemistry, materials design and organic photovoltaics, against GP-based and LLM-enhanced BO baselines, with ablations (the main component ablation is on the HPLC task only per the reviews).
beuggvXtxi.claimed_gains: Better overall performance than GP-based and LLM-enhanced BO baselines across four offline scientific optimization tasks.
beuggvXtxi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework well-motivated and coherent, praising the division of labor between LLM hypothesis generation and GP quantification and the benchmarking on four scientific tasks.
beuggvXtxi.main_concern: Evaluation is limited and possibly unfair: only four offline tasks, ablations on one task, different initial points across baselines, and no comparison with direct history-conditioned hypothesis generation.

JR803D5cQB.one_liner: Learns an offline data-free structural prior over model parameters, then unlearns with a single analytic update and no retain data.
JR803D5cQB.problem: Machine unlearning methods depend on original retain data and are operationally slow, which makes calibrating forgetting intensity and handling concurrent requests hard.
JR803D5cQB.method: PRISM learns a Data-Free Structural Prior offline by modeling the model's intrinsic parameter structure (a VAE over pretrained parameters whose decoder Jacobian indicates parameter importance, per the reviews). At request time it computes a forget-set Fisher and applies one analytical update controlled by a single intensity parameter.
JR803D5cQB.key_idea: Precompute a parameter-importance prior from a VAE over pretrained weights, then solve each unlearning request with one analytic update instead of iterative optimization.
JR803D5cQB.evidence: Class-wise forgetting and nudity-removal experiments across discriminative and generative models, comparing retain and test accuracy with Retrain, request-time computation cost, and ablations such as Table 6.
JR803D5cQB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like separating offline structural modeling from request-time updates, which makes forgetting intensity cheap to calibrate and cuts request-time computation across discriminative and generative unlearning tasks.
JR803D5cQB.main_concern: The structural prior's construction and its link to knowledge retention are insufficiently justified or isolated, since it is unclear why VAE decoder sensitivity reflects parameter importance for retained behavior.

BfiqcTZ7nL.one_liner: Deep Koopman learning in distribution space: learned distributional observables, linear latent dynamics, and a generative map back to distributions.
BfiqcTZ7nL.problem: Systems observed only through unpaired distribution snapshots resist trajectory-based dynamical learning, and infinite-dimensional distribution space makes compact, approximately closed representations hard to learn.
BfiqcTZ7nL.method: DisKO treats the distribution itself as the dynamical state and jointly learns predictive distributional observables, a finite-dimensional Koopman representation, and a generative map back to the full distribution. Per the reviews it combines set encoders, affine latent dynamics and conditional flow matching.
BfiqcTZ7nL.key_idea: Learn finite-dimensional Koopman observables of whole distributions, evolve them with linear latent dynamics, and decode back to distributions with a conditional flow-matching generative map.
BfiqcTZ7nL.evidence: Seven benchmarks covering synthetic systems, physical simulations, cosmology and single-cell data, plus recovery of leading Koopman eigenvalues and eigenfunctions on systems with analytic spectra.
BfiqcTZ7nL.claimed_gains: Best extrapolation performance across seven benchmarks, with substantially slower error accumulation on long-horizon prediction, and no numeric values stated.
BfiqcTZ7nL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling distribution dynamics directly from unpaired snapshots is well motivated and that long-horizon forecasting results are strong across broad benchmarks.
BfiqcTZ7nL.main_concern: The contribution is largely compositional (set encoders, Koopman dynamics, conditional flow matching) and no theory shows that the learned observables form an approximately invariant subspace or that dynamics are identifiable from unpaired snapshots.

4VQacZlySN.one_liner: Rewards reasoning prefixes that let a separate receiver model continue to a correct answer, as an auxiliary signal beside RLVR.
4VQacZlySN.problem: RLVR rewards only final-answer correctness, so equally correct solutions can differ in how useful their intermediate reasoning is.
4VQacZlySN.method: RLTR truncates a generated solution at a prefix and rewards it when a separate receiver model, given that prefix, continues to the correct answer, using this as an auxiliary training reward for the generator.
4VQacZlySN.key_idea: Truncate the generator's reasoning at a prefix and reward it by the probability that a separate frozen receiver model completes it correctly.
4VQacZlySN.evidence: Mathematical, scientific, coding and visual reasoning tasks with multiple backbones, receiver controls, ablations on reward weights, receiver choice and truncation strategy, and three training seeds in the main setup per the reviews.
4VQacZlySN.claimed_gains: +5.8%p in Maj@64 on AMC23 over RLVR, and matches RLVR's average accuracy with roughly 2.5x fewer training steps on MATH-500.
4VQacZlySN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the auxiliary reward simple and easy to implement without a separate reward model, with broad empirical support across backbones, datasets and receiver controls.
4VQacZlySN.main_concern: The mechanism is unclear because receivers may repair prefix errors or adapt to prefix style, so gains may not reflect more reliable reasoning, and the distinction from PAV is only partly isolated.

jESPrGt5Ct.one_liner: Derives sufficient conditions for sublinear counterfactual regret of reflective agents from local generation and deployment guarantees, formalized in Lean.
jESPrGt5Ct.problem: Existing guarantees for policy selection and action generation do not establish when local reflection yields long-term performance guarantees for the complete agent under resource constraints.
jESPrGt5Ct.method: They derive a resource-sensitive transfer that bounds full-state deployment discrepancies along actual execution paths while preserving own-history laws of learner and comparator, plus a cumulative generation opportunity bound trading off quality, coverage and hard budget. A SQL reporting example illustrates the conditions, and all eighteen numbered results are formalized in Lean.
jESPrGt5Ct.key_idea: Bound full-state deployment discrepancy along actual execution paths and combine it with a cumulative generation opportunity bound, keeping the native controller, to obtain sublinear counterfactual regret.
jESPrGt5Ct.evidence: Theory with a Lean formalization of the conditional proof chain for all eighteen numbered results, including a native instance with repeated policy growth and imperfect validation, plus a SQL reporting example measuring cumulative task loss and resource use.
jESPrGt5Ct.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the modular analysis that separates generation, selection, representation, alignment and deployment errors, and the Lean formalization that supports checking the composed argument.
jESPrGt5Ct.main_concern: Practical applicability is unclear: assumptions such as the controller-reference performance gap are hard to verify, examples are simple, and there is no empirical comparison with methods such as Reflexion or Self-Refine.

l939DWkl8S.one_liner: Turns existing molecule-response pairs into reciprocal preference pairs for preference optimization, adapting molecular LLMs while preserving general capabilities.
l939DWkl8S.problem: Large-scale domain SFT adapts general LLMs to molecular tasks but can overwrite base-model capabilities, degrading general-purpose abilities and molecular reasoning outside the fine-tuning distribution.
l939DWkl8S.method: ReMPA pairs template-aligned, structurally similar molecules so each response is preferred under its own molecular condition and rejected under the other's, which yields preference pairs without human annotation.
