Preference optimization anchored to a reference policy is then applied.
l939DWkl8S.key_idea: Swap responses between template-aligned, structurally similar molecules so each is preferred for its own molecule and rejected for the other, then optimize preferences against a reference policy.
l939DWkl8S.evidence: Molecular property prediction, molecular reasoning and comprehension (MoleculeQA, FGBench), and general-capability evaluation such as MMLU, compared against the unadapted base model and one-way DPO per the reviews.
l939DWkl8S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the preference construction is practical, reusing existing molecule-response supervision without human preference annotation or extra response generation, and that the capability-preservation motivation is meaningful.
l939DWkl8S.main_concern: The reciprocal pairs' pseudo-negatives lack semantic validation because similar molecules can share valid responses, and the benefit of reciprocal construction over plain preference optimization is not cleanly isolated.

rwMLiqEt1z.one_liner: Seals semantic opportunities before policy assignment and reuses them across intervention branches, giving fixed-semantics counterfactual replay for LLM-agent social simulation.
rwMLiqEt1z.problem: In LLM-agent counterfactuals, an intervention that changes platform state alters later prompts and language, so standard replay mixes structural policy response with post-intervention semantic adaptation even with shared seeds.
rwMLiqEt1z.method: They formalize interventions in the Behavior-Platform Decomposed Mechanistic Transition Framework (BDMTF) and introduce Rehydration, a paired replay protocol that generates and seals semantic opportunities before policy assignment and reuses them across branches, defining a fixed-semantics structural effect.
rwMLiqEt1z.key_idea: Generate and seal semantic opportunities before policy assignment, then reuse them across intervention branches so only structural policy effects differ.
rwMLiqEt1z.evidence: An analytic setting with known ground truth where Rehydration recovers the fixed-semantics target and common-seed adaptive replay does not, plus controlled factorial experiments and mechanism-deletion and execution-trace analyses.
rwMLiqEt1z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clear separation of fixed-semantics and adaptive-semantic effects, a carefully specified replay protocol, and extensive mechanistic analysis of the behavior-by-ranking interaction (Shallow Swarm).
rwMLiqEt1z.main_concern: The value of freezing semantics is not well established, since restricted semantic feedback and manually designed phase-II policies narrow what the experiments show and the Shallow Swarm mechanism lacks independent support.

Tfhqza7CH1.one_liner: Species-average bill, tarsus and tail ratios become a morphometric prior, realized as axial part deformations of a parametric bird model.
Tfhqza7CH1.problem: Single-image 3D bird reconstruction methods recover pose and silhouette well but produce part proportions that barely vary across species and do not match measured species proportions.
Tfhqza7CH1.method: Lengths from AVONET (over 90,000 measured individuals across 11,000 species) are expressed as ratios to wing length, and the species-average ratios form the prior. A morphometric pathway realizes it without disturbing the pretrained body model, with a proportion head inferring per-part length factors from pretrained features.
Tfhqza7CH1.key_idea: Express part lengths as ratios to wing length and steer per-part length factors toward species-average ratios through a separate morphometric pathway.
Tfhqza7CH1.evidence: Built on AniMer+ and compared against it on species-level generalization and alternative adaptation approaches, with proportion agreement measured against AVONET species averages and a mesh diagnostic on 678 held-out photographs per the reviews.
Tfhqza7CH1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using ornithological measurements as a species-level prior is well motivated, that the method is lightweight, and that the evaluation clearly shows differences from the AniMer+ baseline.
Tfhqza7CH1.main_concern: The comparison is mainly against AniMer+ and measures agreement with species averages rather than per-image accuracy, while mesh diagnostics show defects such as gate failures on 20.2% of held-out images.

3hukpUdtbw.one_liner: Refines few-step diffusion timesteps by minimizing reference feature-mean discrepancy, an unbiased U-statistic proxy for local FID, without retraining.
3hukpUdtbw.problem: Few-step diffusion schedules are optimized for numerical or trajectory-level accuracy while quality is judged in a nonlinear feature space, so schedules with similar state-space error can have very different FID.
3hukpUdtbw.method: The feature-mean discrepancy to a high-accuracy reference (the mean component of FID to the reference) serves as a local schedule-refinement objective, estimated with an unbiased U-statistic that removes the paired feature-dispersion term of the naive plug-in estimator. The method needs neither model retraining nor real-data statistics during schedule search.
3hukpUdtbw.key_idea: Optimize timesteps locally against the feature-mean discrepancy to a high-accuracy reference, estimated with an unbiased U-statistic, because that term tracks the local FID landscape.
3hukpUdtbw.evidence: Eight pixel-space settings spanning three datasets, four solvers and 4-16 NFE (CIFAR-10, FFHQ and AFHQv2 per the reviews), plus a Stable Diffusion experiment, compared with other objectives under matched initialization and search budget.
3hukpUdtbw.claimed_gains: Schedules lie 0.47-4.13% above best-found direct-FID solutions (median 1.78%), versus median gaps of 16.48% for paired feature... (abstract truncated).
3hukpUdtbw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a meaningful mismatch between numerical error and FID-oriented quality and offers a simple, training-free objective supported by theoretical and empirical analysis across datasets, solvers and budgets.
3hukpUdtbw.main_concern: Search cost is high and the local justification depends on starting from an already reasonable schedule, with evaluation focused mainly on FID.

oTVdnpii0z.one_liner: Casts token-level LLM watermarks as solutions to one constrained optimization problem, unifying KGW, AAR/KTH and SynthID.
oTVdnpii0z.problem: There is no general, principled formulation of token-level LLM watermarking that explains current schemes or eases designing new ones.
oTVdnpii0z.method: A constrained optimization formulation under which most popular token-level watermarks are solutions, each optimizing a different constraint, which exposes a quality-diversity-power trade-off. Schemes derived from a chosen constraint can target specific requirements such as minimizing perplexity.
oTVdnpii0z.key_idea: Frame each watermark as maximizing expected token score under a constraint on the sampling distribution, so different constraints recover existing schemes and new ones.
oTVdnpii0z.evidence: Experiments show that schemes derived from a given constraint maximize detection power for that constraint, across several LLMs and settings including detection and text quality, per the abstract and reviews.
oTVdnpii0z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the constrained-optimization framework neatly unifies KGW, AAR/KTH and SynthID, explains what each method optimizes, and yields a practical new scheme.
oTVdnpii0z.main_concern: Support for the optimality claims is incomplete (maximizing expected score need not maximize detection power at a fixed false-positive rate), and the evaluation protocol and inference overhead of the new scheme are weakly characterized.

9opSJ7Vfff.one_liner: Benchmark and VLM judge for long, multi-region visual text replacement, plus GlyphPlan, which plans line layouts before rendering glyph conditions.
9opSJ7Vfff.problem: Image editors handle short word swaps, but real updates involve long text, source-to-target length changes and multiple jointly edited regions, and existing benchmarks do not isolate these challenges.
9opSJ7Vfff.method: ReflowText is an English-to-English, replacement-only benchmark with 2,002 images and 9,197 regions, scored with OCR metrics and the fine-tuned VLM judge ReflowJudge. GlyphPlan has a fine-tuned VLM predict line-level layouts, a deterministic renderer create spatially aligned glyph conditions, and the image editor restore visual appearance.
9opSJ7Vfff.key_idea: Predict line-level text layouts with a fine-tuned VLM first, render them deterministically as glyph conditions, and let the image editor restore appearance.
9opSJ7Vfff.evidence: Benchmark evaluation of 14 recent editors per the reviews, GlyphPlan tested on two open-weight backbones, and ReflowJudge checked against human annotations.
9opSJ7Vfff.claimed_gains: ReflowJudge reaches 79.1% agreement with human annotations, and GlyphPlan consistently improves aggregate quality, especially font style and layout, across two open-weight backbones.
9opSJ7Vfff.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a real gap in long-form, length-mismatched, multi-region text editing and that the combined OCR and VLM-judge evaluation is useful.
9opSJ7Vfff.main_concern: No results are broken down by text length, length mismatch or number of regions, so the three difficulty axes are described but not tested, and GlyphPlan's necessity versus simpler baselines is unproven.

BPjeXqtWLD.one_liner: Recurrent PEFT repeatedly runs a frozen pretrained middle stack with lightweight adapters, raising effective depth without adding backbone parameters.
BPjeXqtWLD.problem: Most PEFT methods add adaptation capacity by changing how parameters modify a fixed pretrained computation graph, leaving the amount of pretrained computation itself untouched.
BPjeXqtWLD.method: Recurrent PEFT executes a frozen pretrained middle stack repeatedly while training lightweight adapters around the reused computation, using residual damped recurrence from prior work, with iteration-specific and iteration-shared adaptation. It is compared with single-pass PEFT at matched trainable-parameter budgets.
BPjeXqtWLD.key_idea: Treat computational depth as an adaptation variable by looping a frozen middle layer stack with adapters, either specific to each iteration or shared across iterations.
BPjeXqtWLD.evidence: Qwen and Llama backbones from 0.6B to 8B parameters on general reasoning, GSM8K and Minerva, with ablations of PEFT parameterization and recurrence formulation.
BPjeXqtWLD.claimed_gains: Broadly competitive on general reasoning with gains on GSM8K across all evaluated backbones, and substantially larger Minerva gains on Qwen than on Llama, with no numbers stated.
BPjeXqtWLD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framing clean, with matched trainable-parameter budgets and careful controls, and appreciate the analysis of initialization stability and damping formulation.
BPjeXqtWLD.main_concern: Baselines look undertrained or miscalibrated (low learning rate, implausibly low fine-tuned scores), and the idea is a modest extension of existing looped-transformer plus LoRA work.

zQ3tqHPwi3.one_liner: Trains a value-aware indexer to pick KV anchors in one scoring pass, then merges keys and fits compact values.
zQ3tqHPwi3.problem: Iterative anchor search dominates the compaction cost of OMP-based Attention Matching for long, reusable context prefixes whose KV caches grow linearly with sequence length.
zQ3tqHPwi3.method: A value-aware indexer is trained to select real-key anchors in a single scoring pass, then ARC-KV applies convex-hull-constrained key merging and fits an attention-mass bias and compact values against the full cache. The compact cache is built once per context with the frozen indexer and reused for all later queries.
zQ3tqHPwi3.key_idea: Selective amortization: learn a reusable anchor-selection policy across contexts while keeping context-specific reconstruction through key merging and closed-form fitting of bias and values.
zQ3tqHPwi3.evidence: QuALITY, RULER and LongBench on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct against reported compaction methods including OMP-based Attention Matching, plus an additional model study at one retention ratio per the reviews.
zQ3tqHPwi3.claimed_gains: Outperforms reported compaction methods in most settings, and at 10% KV retention on QuALITY improves accuracy from 0.6409 to 0.6520 over Attention Matching (abstract truncated after this point).
zQ3tqHPwi3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that replacing iterative anchor search with a learned scoring indexer cuts compaction cost while keeping accuracy, with broad evaluation across benchmarks, models and retention ratios.
zQ3tqHPwi3.main_concern: The learned indexer's contribution is not isolated from the other components (non-uniform head budgets, key merging, value fitting), and speedups are reported for compaction time only rather than end-to-end latency.

1BBhdrVaZ2.one_liner: Benchmark of 148 day-0 model-support tasks in vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM, scoring coding agents on correctness and serving speed.
1BBhdrVaZ2.problem: It is unclear whether coding agents can implement a new model architecture, integrate it with a serving runtime and optimize kernels so that day-0 model support is both correct and fast.
1BBhdrVaZ2.method: An automated pipeline builds executable environments from model-integration pull requests in vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM, each with correctness checks and an expert performance baseline validated on the target accelerator from NVIDIA, AMD or Google. The pipeline can incorporate new model releases.
1BBhdrVaZ2.key_idea: Rebuild pre-integration engine states from real integration PRs and grade agent patches first on correctness against the maintainers' patch, then on serving speed versus an expert baseline.
1BBhdrVaZ2.evidence: Seven models evaluated on 148 tasks across 10 accelerator tiers, with one trajectory per task per the reviews.
1BBhdrVaZ2.claimed_gains: Agents resolve 56.7% of tasks on average, 33% of resolved patches serve more slowly than the maintainers' implementation by a median of 18%, and the strongest model delivers a correct patch at expert speed on only 52.7% of tasks, with 32% of its resolved patches slower.
1BBhdrVaZ2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely and well scoped and that the extensible pipeline reconstructing real integration tasks across engines and accelerators is the main contribution.
1BBhdrVaZ2.main_concern: Contamination from public pull requests that models may have seen in training is unaddressed, and results use a single trajectory per task without variance reporting.

Mz7VSShqYl.one_liner: Trains a retriever by having an auxiliary LM predict conversation fragments from retriever-weighted context, jointly with MS MARCO contrastive learning.
Mz7VSShqYl.problem: General-purpose embedding models struggle with long-term agent memory retrieval because query-memory relevance labels are rare and costly to obtain.
Mz7VSShqYl.method: MemRevela learns retrieval from dependencies between conversational turns: an auxiliary language model predicts conversational fragments using retriever-weighted context, so its prediction loss trains the retriever, which is then jointly optimized with standard MS MARCO contrastive learning.
Mz7VSShqYl.key_idea: Weight context by retriever scores when an auxiliary LM predicts neighboring conversation fragments, so the prediction loss supervises the retriever without relevance labels.
Mz7VSShqYl.evidence: Five model sizes from 0.1B to 8B on LMEB's 22 datasets across four memory types, downstream QA over long conversations against two proprietary embedding APIs, and an embedding-space analysis.
Mz7VSShqYl.claimed_gains: MemRevela-8B reaches a dataset-averaged nDCG@10 of 63.24 without task instructions, exceeding NV-Embed-v2 by 3.43 absolute points.
Mz7VSShqYl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated, that unlabeled conversational dependencies are a fitting supervision source, and that the setup is robust and reproducible, with a drop-in retriever that needs no extra inference cost.
Mz7VSShqYl.main_concern: Gains are modest and the central claim is not isolated, since the training mechanism comes from Revela and no compute-matched generic-text control shows that conversational data is what helps.

bF569Sxzvn.one_liner: Trains a small per-source editor from reward and prior feedback, keeping the pretrained backbone out of the inner optimization loop.
bF569Sxzvn.problem: Test-time reward-guided image editing methods optimize candidates through pretrained generation processes, so repeated adjustment depends on costly large-model execution and sometimes backbone backpropagation.
bF569Sxzvn.method: A theoretical framework jointly accounts for reward, source preservation and pretrained-prior preferences. FASTER trains a small network per source and objective while pretrained and reward models give feedback on candidate outputs, reusing each candidate and its feedback across several small-network updates.
bF569Sxzvn.key_idea: Train a small per-source network on a stochastic-optimal-control objective, reusing each candidate's endpoint feedback across updates so the backbone stays outside the inner loop.
bF569Sxzvn.evidence: SD3 and Stable Diffusion 1.5 experiments against evaluated baselines, including one that optimizes controls along pretrained generation trajectories, with an extensive appendix per the reviews.
bF569Sxzvn.claimed_gains: On SD3, FASTER leads all four target metrics and several validation metrics, with editing-time speedups of up to 6.91x on Stable Diffusion 3 and 24.14x on Stable Diffusion 1.5 over the baseline that optimizes controls along pretrained generation trajectories.
bF569Sxzvn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find decoupling the editor from the generative backbone sensible and appealing, with an extensive appendix and a useful adaptation of stochastic optimal control to test-time editing.
bF569Sxzvn.main_concern: Technical novelty is modest because adjoint matching, endpoint feedback reuse and the semantic editing term follow prior work, and per-technique ablations are missing.

NDNTmpXIBj.one_liner: Reinforcement-learned policy selects transferable source-domain subsets for molecular OOD property prediction, followed by dual-scale adaptation.
NDNTmpXIBj.problem: Scaffold splits leave structural overlap that overstates molecular OOD extrapolation, and indiscriminate alignment across heterogeneous source domains can cause negative transfer under severe distribution shift.
NDNTmpXIBj.method: SCOPE-Bench partitions molecules by clusters in a physicochemical descriptor space. POMA learns a policy that selects transferable source subsets from a large candidate pool and then applies dual-scale adaptation capturing global molecular topology and local pharmacophore patterns; per the reviews the policy is trained with GRPO using structurally similar labeled scaffolds as proxy targets.
NDNTmpXIBj.key_idea: Train a source-selection policy with proxy rewards from structurally related labeled scaffolds standing in for the unlabeled target, so downstream adaptation performance guides selection.
NDNTmpXIBj.evidence: SCOPE-Bench with three 3D backbones and three properties (nine combinations) and 15 target-scaffold tasks, compared with a supervised model trained on all source data and other adaptation methods per the reviews.
NDNTmpXIBj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that source selection to avoid negative transfer is a meaningful problem and that SCOPE-Bench and the proxy-reward idea are reasonable and may inspire follow-up work.
NDNTmpXIBj.main_concern: The method is computationally heavy (about 72 GPU-hours offline plus about 4.5 GPU-hours per target scaffold), the benchmark excludes rare scaffolds, and the methodological contribution is seen as incremental.

RM7paXamDX.one_liner: Scores prompt token importance with upper-layer attention from learnable latent tokens, trained by RL rewarding answers and evidence preservation.
RM7paXamDX.problem: Prompt compressors introduce semantic distortion and hallucination by underestimating reasoning-critical tokens or overrating superficial word matches, and answer-level supervision gives only indirect guidance.
RM7paXamDX.method: Learnable latent tokens appended to the question act as implicit reasoning states, and upper-layer attention from them isolates relational reasoning signals from lexical noise to estimate token importance. The compressor is trained with reinforcement learning that jointly rewards answer correctness and supporting-evidence preservation.
RM7paXamDX.key_idea: Use upper-layer latent-to-document attention from learnable latent tokens as the token-importance signal, trained with anchor-conditioned RL rewarding answers and supporting evidence.
RM7paXamDX.evidence: Question-answering and long-context benchmarks (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA and MuSiQue with two generators per the reviews), with component ablations and evidence-preservation analyses.
RM7paXamDX.claimed_gains: Retaining only 10% of tokens, BridgeComp improves Exact Match by up to 62.44% over the strongest baseline (the long-context result is truncated in the abstract).
RM7paXamDX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree improvements are consistent across datasets, compression budgets and downstream generators, supported by substantial ablations and evidence-preservation analyses, with clear writing.
RM7paXamDX.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited because the method combines latent tokens, attention aggregation and RL, and baseline fairness is unclear since BridgeComp uses extra gold supporting-evidence supervision.

Ptuhr3yDfH.one_liner: Rounds calibrated conformal thresholds up to a pre-agreed shared grid so independent agents deploy identical prediction sets.
Ptuhr3yDfH.problem: Two agents calibrating the same model on their own data compute different continuous thresholds and deploy different prediction sets, so predictions cannot be reused or audited across agents.
Ptuhr3yDfH.method: Each calibrated threshold is rounded up to the nearest of a few pre-agreed values (a grid in coverage units of a public score distribution), so both agents deploy identical sets with a chosen probability while each keeps its own coverage guarantee, at the cost of larger prediction sets. They prove identical sets are impossible without shared information, a shared seed enables them at an unavoidable worst-case cost for seed-based rules, and a small public sample removes the seed and lowers the cost.
Ptuhr3yDfH.key_idea: Round each split-conformal cutoff up onto a shared grid defined in coverage units of a public score sample, so independent calibrations land on the same threshold.
Ptuhr3yDfH.evidence: Theory covering impossibility without shared information, a seed-based lower bound, and guarantees for every continuous score distribution with a public sample, plus experiments on ImageNet, CIFAR-100 and four language models (GPT-2, Pythia, Qwen, Llama).
Ptuhr3yDfH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and the theory solid, with simple methods that keep each side's coverage guarantee even when the shared public sample is unrepresentative.
Ptuhr3yDfH.main_concern: The practical importance of exact agreement is weakly motivated, since independently calibrated models may already agree closely and a representative public pilot sample may be hard to obtain.

R68bChiwfq.one_liner: Two-phase post-training for VLM visual number sense: configuration coverage first, then relational numerosity supervision with multi-interface counting and comparison.
R68bChiwfq.problem: Vision-language models are sensitive to quantity, but their ability to answer numerical questions remains uneven across visual scenes and tasks.
R68bChiwfq.method: Phase one, Configuration Coverage, associates shared count labels with complementary object layouts and appearances. Phase two combines Relational Numerosity Supervision, linking counts through local changes and part-whole relations, with multi-interface supervision for comparison and query-conditioned counting, using a controlled synthetic dataset.
R68bChiwfq.key_idea: First tie shared count labels to varied layouts and appearances, then supervise counts through local changes and part-whole relations across several task interfaces.
R68bChiwfq.evidence: Two VLM families (Qwen and InternVL per the reviews) on a controlled synthetic dataset and external numerical benchmarks such as PixMo-Count, with matched-budget ablations, supervision-allocation studies and representation analyses.
R68bChiwfq.claimed_gains: Substantial improvements in synthetic counting and task-dependent gains on external numerical benchmarks, with no numbers stated.
R68bChiwfq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the systematic decomposition into configuration, cardinality and task, with each component contributing to a different aspect of numerical performance, plus informative representation analyses and a reusable synthetic dataset.
R68bChiwfq.main_concern: Component attribution is confounded and incomplete (extra Coverage data in the full model, partial factorial design), and gains on natural images are far smaller than on the authors' synthetic data.

zLrqJ7xbMS.one_liner: Trains LLM graders with correctness labels on original answers plus equivalence supervision, so equivalent variants get the same rubric judgments.
zLrqJ7xbMS.problem: LLM graders of open-ended student responses change their judgments under construct-irrelevant variation (rubric drift), even when questions, rubrics and rubric-relevant evidence are fixed.
zLrqJ7xbMS.method: EduR2Bench provides 1,060 verified rubric-equivalence groups and 3,297 variants across four STEM subjects, with the label-free Criterion Flip Rate (CFR) as a drift diagnostic. RITE (Rubric-Invariant Training via Equivalence) combines correctness grounding with equivalence supervision, using labels only on original responses.
zLrqJ7xbMS.key_idea: Combine correctness supervision on original responses with an equivalence objective over verified rubric-equivalent variants, so grading invariance is trained explicitly.
zLrqJ7xbMS.evidence: EduR2Bench across open-weight, frontier and specialized graders, with a second backbone, a held-out transformation family, unseen human-written rewrites, and supervision and noise analyses.
zLrqJ7xbMS.claimed_gains: Correctness supervision reduces CFR on unsupervised equivalent variants from 26.3% to 11.7%, and RITE reduces CFR to 5.2% while preserving grading quality.
zLrqJ7xbMS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is well controlled with verified equivalence groups and separates invariance from correctness, with comprehensive experiments across subjects, backbones and human-written variants.
zLrqJ7xbMS.main_concern: The advance over prior work on consistency under meaning-preserving variation is not clearly established, and the validity of the scoring criteria underlying the benchmark needs stronger evidence.

2xy815Qm47.one_liner: Routes shared image-level style to state-transition dynamics and token-varying style to input writes in a pretrained Diffusion-Mamba denoiser.
2xy815Qm47.problem: Reference-based image style transfer methods struggle to transfer both global appearance and local stylistic details while preserving content structure.
2xy815Qm47.method: GASC assigns shared image-level style conditioning to state-transition dynamics and token-varying style carriers to input writes in a pretrained Diffusion-Mamba denoiser. Per-head orthogonal residualization reduces content interference in reference features, content-conditioned carrier retrieval captures local style, and a separate content stream anchors spatial structure.
2xy815Qm47.key_idea: Match style granularity to the SSM conditioning interface: global style drives state transitions and spatially varying style drives input writes, after orthogonally removing content from reference features.
2xy815Qm47.evidence: Comparisons against existing style transfer methods using FID, ArtFID, CFSD and LPIPS, with a 2x2 granularity allocation study, single-route ablations and visual comparisons per the reviews.
2xy815Qm47.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing methods in overall stylization quality while maintaining competitive content preservation, with no numbers stated.
2xy815Qm47.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the architecture is coherent and that the 2x2 allocation study and ablations directly test its central hypothesis, with the best FID, ArtFID and CFSD among evaluated methods.
2xy815Qm47.main_concern: Novelty is incremental over existing Diffusion-Mamba and Mamba-based style transfer, and content-preservation evidence is mixed (worse LPIPS than the strongest content-oriented baseline) with no human preference study.

ozlyimTagV.one_liner: Matches frames to a reference with degradation-robust features, warps it into per-frame guidance, and distills from a full-reference teacher.
ozlyimTagV.problem: Simply appending reference frames to a video diffusion transformer leaves much of the reference unused even when reliable correspondences exist, so generative video restoration still hallucinates inconsistent textures.
ozlyimTagV.method: MatchVR is a one-step reference-guided generative restoration framework with degradation-robust feature matching to estimate dense target-reference correspondences and confidence, a spatiotemporal reference alignment module that warps and relocates matched content to each target frame, and aligned-reference distillation from a full-reference teacher.
ozlyimTagV.key_idea: Convert one reference frame into dense, frame-specific matched guidance via robust correspondence and warping instead of concatenating it to the video transformer input.
ozlyimTagV.evidence: Multiple benchmarks (including SPMCS and UDM10 per the reviews) measuring PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS across varying temporal distances, with ground-truth-first-frame and restored-reference settings.
ozlyimTagV.claimed_gains: Consistently improves reference utilization and restoration quality across varying temporal distances, with no numbers stated in the visible abstract.
ozlyimTagV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis of a reference utilization gap is clear and intuitive and that the method gives consistent gains over concatenation-based reference guidance.
ozlyimTagV.main_concern: Headline gains rely on the ground-truth first-frame reference, fidelity is not consistently better than a blind restoration baseline when using a restored reference, and quality depends heavily on reference quality.

M5uDpybt2w.one_liner: Pre-rollout RLVR batch selector: KL-regularized domain quotas, then within-domain selection that penalizes how chosen cases interact.
M5uDpybt2w.problem: Multi-domain RLVR can produce unstable policy updates, because selecting high-scoring cases independently overlooks the risk of using them together and favoring some domains limits learning of other capabilities.
M5uDpybt2w.method: TaylorMix first allocates domain quotas by KL-regularized allocation that balances domain priorities with continued opportunities across capabilities, then selects cases within each domain using companion-dependent scores that account for composition risk through a geometric penalty. Selection happens before rollout and leaves GRPO unchanged.
M5uDpybt2w.key_idea: Allocate per-domain quotas with a KL-regularized objective, then pick cases sequentially using a Taylor-motivated geometric penalty conditioned on previously selected companions.
M5uDpybt2w.evidence: Matched-budget training on two Qwen backbones across mathematical reasoning, code and general capability, with ablations of both balance levels and theory quantifying the allocation trade-off and conditional geometric-penalty reduction.
M5uDpybt2w.claimed_gains: Highest category means among the compared methods in mathematical reasoning, code and general capability on two evaluated backbones, with fewer large gradient spikes and zero-advantage rollout groups in the observed trajectories.
M5uDpybt2w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the two-level, pre-rollout batch construction practical and low-overhead, with consistent gains across capability categories and backbones and useful ablations.
M5uDpybt2w.main_concern: The benefit of companion-dependent selection is not cleanly isolated from individual geometric filtering, and the theory characterizes the method's own objectives without showing that the penalty reflects actual update behavior.

Mzkyz1Xth3.one_liner: An independent human pathway plus a human-conditioned camera generator unifies camera-from-human and joint generation, with learned camera translation-intensity control.
Mzkyz1Xth3.problem: Camera generation for a given human motion and joint human-camera generation are treated as separate tasks, and translation intensity stays underspecified by human context and camera text.
Mzkyz1Xth3.method: AESOP has an independent human pathway and a shared human-conditioned camera generator that serves both tasks while preserving the human output. It builds trajectory pairs that differ in camera translation magnitude while sharing human motion and camera text, and uses them to learn an explicit intensity condition.
Mzkyz1Xth3.key_idea: Generate human motion independently, condition the camera generator on it, and learn translation intensity from trajectory pairs that differ only in translation magnitude.
Mzkyz1Xth3.evidence: Experiments on the PulpMotion dataset for both tasks, with a 29-participant user study, comparisons against PulpMotion DiT and MAR baselines, and intensity-control tests per the reviews.
Mzkyz1Xth3.claimed_gains: Strong camera distributional and framing quality in both tasks and effective control over camera translation intensity, with no numbers stated.
Mzkyz1Xth3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the asymmetric human-first formulation simple, practical and useful, and consider the results, including the user study, and the intensity-paired augmentation convincing.
Mzkyz1Xth3.main_concern: The asymmetric architecture's contribution is not cleanly isolated from other differences versus PulpMotion, baseline framing guidance is disabled, and translation-intensity control is only partly validated.

4hKEm53XQF.one_liner: Output-side rectifier confines hyperspectral super-resolution corrections to a learned compact spectral subspace, trained per backbone.
4hKEm53XQF.problem: HSI-SR backbones improve spatial reconstruction but leave residual spectral errors, and architecture-bound spectral treatments must be rebuilt for every new backbone.
4hKEm53XQF.method: SR2-Net needs only a backbone's output and follows an enhance-then-rectify pipeline: Hierarchical Spectral-Spatial Synergy Attention (H-S3A) reinforces cross-band interactions and Mode-Constrained Rectification (MCR) confines correction to a learned compact spectral subspace. A degradation-consistency constraint ties the output to the observed low-resolution input.
4hKEm53XQF.key_idea: Project the correction onto a few learned spectral modes outside the backbone, exploiting low-dimensional spectral structure that belongs to the data rather than to any architecture.
4hKEm53XQF.evidence: Experiments with five backbones from three families at three scales, in-domain and cross-domain tests, a frozen-backbone variant, and test-time degradation mismatch per the reviews.
4hKEm53XQF.claimed_gains: Improves spectral fidelity on CNN, Transformer and diffusion HSI-SR backbones, with no numbers visible in the truncated abstract.
4hKEm53XQF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the insight that low-dimensional spectral structure belongs to the data interesting and the experiments extensive, with a lightweight design that plugs into existing models.
4hKEm53XQF.main_concern: The model-agnostic claim is overstated because the rectifier is retrained per backbone, and the method is of limited novelty with a weakly justified low-rank assumption for residual errors.

kKowbMDmjh.one_liner: Benchmark of 118 law-discovery problems: held-out fit on real data, plus recovery of a synthesized equation variant via simulator queries.
kKowbMDmjh.problem: Evaluating whether LLMs discover scientific laws requires moving beyond familiar published equations while keeping tasks grounded in scientific data and constraints.
kKowbMDmjh.method: SciLaws-Bench packages 118 problems across six disciplines from 381 papers, 291 candidate laws and roughly 8M data points, each linking a problem, data, reference equations and scientific-validity rubrics. SciLaws-Real scores proposed laws on held-out fit and scientific validity, and SciLaws-Parallel scores recovery of a newly synthesized structural variant through active queries to a simulator calibrated to the source data.
kKowbMDmjh.key_idea: Pair real-data evaluation with a parallel setting where a published equation gets a synthesized structural variant that must be recovered by querying a data-calibrated simulator.
kKowbMDmjh.evidence: Fourteen models evaluated with judge prompts, blinded expert validation and cold-recall controls per the reviews.
kKowbMDmjh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is valuable and well documented, separates fitting observations from discovering scientifically valid laws, and is evaluated rigorously across many models.
kKowbMDmjh.main_concern: Novelty over closely related benchmarks such as LLM-SRBench and NewtonBench is limited, and no specialized discovery system such as LLM-SR is evaluated.

1F9HeJ3Hvv.one_liner: Continuously refreshed ECtHR-based benchmark that perturbs case text and adds adversarial opinion challenges to test LLM judgment stability.
1F9HeJ3Hvv.problem: LLMs informing high-stakes rights decisions need reliable judgments when case information is presented differently or when they are challenged by adversarial opinions.
1F9HeJ3Hvv.method: LiveHumanRightsBench draws on long European Court of Human Rights case records and embeds an automated pipeline that paraphrases or summarizes each case to test robustness. It also stress-tests whether models keep their stance under adversarial opinions, including challenger identity cues.
1F9HeJ3Hvv.key_idea: Test judgment reliability with automated paraphrase and summary perturbations of real ECtHR cases and multi-turn adversarial dissent that adds no new evidence.
1F9HeJ3Hvv.evidence: Frontier LLMs evaluated on ECtHR case records under paraphrase, summarization and adversarial-opinion challenges, with reasoning-trace and evaluation-awareness analyses per the reviews.
1F9HeJ3Hvv.claimed_gains: Claude-Opus-4.6 and GPT-5.6-Sol reverse over 90% of their initial judgments within two turns of simple adversarial opinion challenges.
1F9HeJ3Hvv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is timely and practically motivated, with a continuously updatable benchmark grounded in real ECtHR judgments and informative findings such as the AI-safety-researcher identity-cue effect.
1F9HeJ3Hvv.main_concern: The studied phenomena (perturbation sensitivity, adversarial disagreement) are already documented, explanations for the instability are speculative, and only v1.0 results demonstrate the claimed continuous refresh.

28DCVVINO9.one_liner: SAGE replaces SAM's perturbation with Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized gradients and adds gradient-disagreement-scaled isotropic noise, targeting both flatness and alignment.
28DCVVINO9.problem: Sharpness-aware and gradient-alignment methods each target one geometric property of the loss landscape and ignore the other, which the authors argue cannot guarantee low excess risk in multi-distribution learning.
28DCVVINO9.method: An excess-risk decomposition yields an alignment term and a curvature term, and a counterexample shows neither bounds the other. SAGE replaces SAM's gradient-scaled perturbation with the polar factor of each layer's gradient matrix computed via Newton-Schulz iteration, and for the alignment component injects isotropic noise whose magnitude depends on gradient disagreement per the reviews.
28DCVVINO9.key_idea: Perturb along the polar factor of each layer's gradient so all spectral directions get similar magnitude, and scale isotropic noise by gradient disagreement across distributions.
28DCVVINO9.evidence: Five domain generalization benchmarks (DomainBed) and integration with several multi-task learning optimizers per the reviews, plus an excess-risk theory with a counterexample.
28DCVVINO9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the excess-risk decomposition an interesting theoretical perspective and the spectral-aware perturbation well motivated, with competitive results across five domain generalization benchmarks.
28DCVVINO9.main_concern: The method combines existing spectral orthogonalization and noise techniques, zero-mean noise injection is not shown to improve gradient alignment, and empirical evidence that joint optimization is needed is weak.

FXLPTx7osi.one_liner: Graph-flow MIP and Lagrangian relaxation make provably optimal compression-based tokenizer vocabulary selection tractable for large corpora.
FXLPTx7osi.problem: Optimal compression-based tokenization is NP-complete and BPE is heuristic, while the prior MIP formulation suffers a parameter explosion that makes it impractical for solvers such as Gurobi and the greedy algorithm has no optimality guarantee.
FXLPTx7osi.method: A graph-flow MIP formulation substantially reduces decision variables and constraints by representing word segmentations as paths in a DAG. A Lagrangian relaxation based on shortest-path selection further improves scalability.
FXLPTx7osi.key_idea: Model segmentations as DAG flows to shrink the MIP, then use a Lagrangian relaxation that decomposes into independent shortest-path problems plus a top-k selection.
FXLPTx7osi.evidence: Compression and running-time experiments (including Wikitext) and language-model training with 22M-parameter models and 256-token context against BPE per the reviews; the abstract text is truncated.
FXLPTx7osi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the approach clean and simple, with a more compact exact formulation and a scalable, parallelizable Lagrangian method.
FXLPTx7osi.main_concern: Downstream evidence is weak: language-model experiments are small, differences from BPE are within noise, scalability is shown on limited data, and a comparison to ConvexTok is missing.

GnPnbu3zTm.one_liner: A brief warm-up on abstract stack-manipulation sequences before language pretraining improves later multi-hop QA without changing perplexity.
GnPnbu3zTm.problem: Warm-up on abstract algorithmic data can help pretraining from random initialization, but its effects on downstream capabilities are not captured by language-modeling perplexity.
GnPnbu3zTm.method: Models first train on an abstract stack task, processing push and pop operations and predicting the remaining contents, using about 1% as many tokens as the language-pretraining phase that follows, then fine-tune on multi-hop QA. Controls include a matched first-in-first-out task, a STACKRAND variant, timing changes and weight interventions.
GnPnbu3zTm.key_idea: Teach a small model a last-in-first-out stack task before language pretraining, which seeds computation that helps dependent reasoning chains rather than perplexity.
GnPnbu3zTm.evidence: Small language models (SmolLM-135M per the reviews) fine-tuned on MuSiQue, HotpotQA and 2WikiMultihopQA, with controlled experiments on task structure, timing and weight interventions.
GnPnbu3zTm.claimed_gains: Improves multi-hop QA after fine-tuning by up to 3.9 F1 points on MuSiQue, with additional gains on HotpotQA and 2WikiMultihopQA, using about 1% as many tokens as language pretraining and despite comparable perplexity.
GnPnbu3zTm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the separation between language-modeling loss and downstream multi-hop gains is the clearest result, supported by targeted control experiments and multiple seeds.
GnPnbu3zTm.main_concern: The mechanism behind the transfer remains unclear, since the STACK, QUEUE and STACKRAND comparisons and timing experiments do not isolate why the warm-up helps.

8WSSP4q5f7.one_liner: Inserts an MLP compression block with node-importance-scaled Gaussian noise between GNN encoder and explainer head, implicitly enforcing an information bottleneck.
8WSSP4q5f7.problem: Explicit variational information-bottleneck losses in GNN explainers give little benefit beyond standard training and are invariant to the joint structure of the selected subgraph.
8WSSP4q5f7.method: BottleneckMLP is a model-agnostic module between the GNN encoder and the explainer head, made of an MLP compression block and a noise component that injects Gaussian noise inversely scaled by node importance. It replaces explicit variational IB losses without performance loss.
8WSSP4q5f7.key_idea: Replace explicit IB loss terms with an MLP compression block plus Gaussian noise scaled inversely to node importance, which implicitly compresses unimportant nodes.
8WSSP4q5f7.evidence: Experiments across multiple explainers, datasets and tasks with ablations and architectural comparisons per the reviews, plus theory decomposing variational IB regularizers and bounding input dependence under the noise.
8WSSP4q5f7.claimed_gains: Replaces explicit variational IB losses without performance loss, with no numbers stated in the visible abstract.
8WSSP4q5f7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the analysis of the limitations of explicit variational IB objectives and find the module simple and pluggable into different GNN explanation frameworks, with thorough experiments.
8WSSP4q5f7.main_concern: The theory does not connect compression to explanation faithfulness and assumes a fixed noise channel unlike the implemented importance-scaled noise, and the experiments do not fully isolate the module's contribution.

kvV3Y8hW6z.one_liner: A geometry expert predicts scene-geometry latents by flow matching, reading video and action states one-way, and is removed at deployment.
kvV3Y8hW6z.problem: World action models learn robot policies from video prediction and action generation, but predicting visual appearance does not explicitly encourage representations of how scene geometry evolves.
kvV3Y8hW6z.method: A frozen 3D foundation model and a spatiotemporal geometry VAE turn multi-camera video windows into geometry latent sequences, which a geometry expert predicts through flow matching. Asymmetric attention lets the geometry expert read video and action representations while neither of those experts reads geometry, so the geometry branch can be omitted at deployment.
kvV3Y8hW6z.key_idea: Geometry gradient transfer: the geometry expert attends to video and action representations but not vice versa, so its loss backpropagates into the deployed experts without creating a geometry dependency.
kvV3Y8hW6z.evidence: LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus comparisons with matched and published baselines such as FastWAM and DreamWAM, a detach ablation and static-geometry controls per the reviews.
kvV3Y8hW6z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the mechanism simple, with the detach ablation acting as a precise causal test, and value the clear separation of training-time geometry supervision from inference-time conditioning.
kvV3Y8hW6z.main_concern: Robustness claims rest on single-run margins and on published rather than matched baselines (no matched LIBERO-Plus run), with no repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

3klNF8Ee7s.one_liner: PASS scores quantile separation per node, using one criterion for both ordering and parent recovery beyond additive-noise models.
3klNF8Ee7s.problem: Uncertainty-based causal discovery methods rely on additive-noise assumptions.
3klNF8Ee7s.method: The Pairwise Average Separation Score (PASS) measures uncertainty through quantile separation, and under a quantile-separation condition the same nodewise score drives both topological ordering and parent recovery. Graph-recovery consistency is established for a growing tensor-spline estimator, including heavy-tailed noise under fractional-moment conditions.
3klNF8Ee7s.key_idea: Measure conditional uncertainty by quantile separation and reuse the same nodewise score to find the topological order and then recover parents.
3klNF8Ee7s.evidence: Consistency theory for tensor-spline estimation, and experiments on additive-noise, heteroskedastic-noise and heavy-tailed (Cauchy, Pareto) settings with three real-data benchmarks.
3klNF8Ee7s.claimed_gains: Robust graph recovery across additive-noise, heteroskedastic-noise and heavy-tailed settings, with evaluations on three real-data benchmarks and no numbers stated.
3klNF8Ee7s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the quantile-separation criterion extends uncertainty-based causal discovery beyond additive noise and finite variance, with a conceptually simple single score, identification and consistency results, and heavy-tailed experiments.
3klNF8Ee7s.main_concern: The consistency theory covers a different estimator (growing full tensor splines) than the one implemented (fixed additive splines, data-dependent thresholds), and ordering depends on variable scales and degrades after rescaling.

8QDDA81MPr.one_liner: Maps LLM-judge confidence scores onto a common Uniform(0,1) scale with a kernel-based Gaussian CDF transform, restoring comparability across candidate counts.
8QDDA81MPr.problem: Confidence-thresholding guarantees for LLM judges assume higher confidence means lower disagreement risk, but confidence scales differ across varying numbers of candidate responses, which can violate monotonicity and invalidate the guarantees.
8QDDA81MPr.method: A kernel-based Gaussian CDF transformation calibrates confidence scores across heterogeneous candidate sizes, and the authors show it approximately maps raw scores onto a common Uniform(0,1) scale.
8QDDA81MPr.key_idea: Pass raw judge confidence through a kernel-based Gaussian CDF transformation so scores from different candidate counts follow a common, approximately uniform scale.
8QDDA81MPr.evidence: Six datasets and eleven judge models per the reviews, covering confidence-agreement monotonicity and coverage under cascade configurations, with multi-candidate labels built by adding randomly sampled alternatives to the preferred response.
8QDDA81MPr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that non-comparable confidence across candidate counts is a practical issue and that the CDF correction is lightweight and simple, applied without retraining, with consistent gains across datasets and judge models.
8QDDA81MPr.main_concern: The guarantee argument is not adequately justified (fixed-sequence testing validity does not rely on monotonicity, and uniformity does not imply monotonic correctness), and multi-candidate ground-truth labels are constructed rather than human-annotated.

AuhSYSUfO6.one_liner: Lightweight router, trained on counterfactual likelihood advantages, selects and mixes generated memory candidates around a direct Engram retrieval anchor.
AuhSYSUfO6.problem: Learned-memory methods read useful memory from a stored table, and it is unclear whether memory can instead be generated and when generated memory helps or interferes with direct retrieval.
AuhSYSUfO6.method: MemoryAthena offers three pathways: direct Engram retrieval (E), generation from retrieved cues (GE), and generation from backbone states without the memory table (GH). With backbone, memory, generators and readers frozen, a causal routing head is trained from counterfactual future-token likelihood advantages of GE and GH relative to E; an admitted candidate modifies the E residual by bounded interpolation, and rejection recovers E exactly.
AuhSYSUfO6.key_idea: Treat direct retrieval as an anchor and train a router on counterfactual future-token likelihood gains of generated candidates, admitting them only through bounded interpolation.
AuhSYSUfO6.evidence: Question answering and other NLP tasks with a frozen backbone, comparing routing and fusion rules on the same checkpoint, with random-router and from-scratch controls and transfer and HaluEval diagnostics per the reviews.
AuhSYSUfO6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is well motivated and that E-anchored asymmetric routing with exact fallback is a sensible, safe design supported by controlled routing comparisons.
AuhSYSUfO6.main_concern: Gains are small and fragile (no seeds or confidence intervals, a threshold tuned on test data, some tasks barely move), and the distinction from existing memory readers and adapters is unclear.

Rb1LMtqN7M.one_liner: Training-free streaming 3D KV cache: leverage-and-attention token retention plus layer-wise budgets from key statistics.
Rb1LMtqN7M.problem: Streaming visual geometry transformers with a fixed KV cache budget must retain scene context, but existing methods treat token importance and key-space diversity independently and ignore the distribution of cached keys.
Rb1LMtqN7M.method: DiaStream combines Important-Distinctive Caching (IDC), which keeps tokens that are both distinctive and reconstruction-relevant using statistical leverage and attention-based importance, with Key Statistics-Aware Budget Allocation (KABA), which allocates the global cache budget across layers by layer-wise key statistics.
Rb1LMtqN7M.key_idea: Retain tokens by statistical leverage combined with attention importance, and split the global KV budget across layers according to each layer's key statistics.
Rb1LMtqN7M.evidence: Multiple streaming 3D reconstruction benchmarks (including 7-Scenes and NRGBD per the reviews) for 3D reconstruction and camera pose estimation, compared with memory-bounded methods such as OVGGT, with component ablations.
Rb1LMtqN7M.claimed_gains: Outperforms existing memory-bounded methods in 3D reconstruction and camera pose estimation while requiring at most 30% of the KV cache budget used by previous methods.
Rb1LMtqN7M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically important and that the training-free method gives strong reconstruction and pose results against bounded-cache baselines, with supporting component ablations.
Rb1LMtqN7M.main_concern: The cache budget can be exceeded to preserve anchor tokens without quantifying actual occupancy, which weakens the cache-saving claim, and the method looks like an elaborate combination of existing cache-management techniques.

Aktxw1WEaI.one_liner: Learns a Bayesian posterior for refining a frozen LLM's predictions from its logits across semantically equivalent prompts.
Aktxw1WEaI.problem: LLM predictive distributions remain sensitive to semantically equivalent prompts, although the variation across such prompts can carry information for predictive refinement.
Aktxw1WEaI.method: CITP uses a small labeled calibration set from the target task to learn a posterior over how to refine predictions from the model's logit responses across semantically equivalent prompts. It then averages predictive distributions over this posterior to account for uncertainty in the learned refinement.
Aktxw1WEaI.key_idea: Fit a Bayesian refinement on contrasts between logit responses to equivalent prompts, and average predictions over the learned posterior.
Aktxw1WEaI.evidence: Three model families and nine tasks spanning fixed-label classification and multiple-choice QA, with scale-and-bias and shuffled-contrast controls and a comparison with BayesPE per the reviews.
Aktxw1WEaI.claimed_gains: Best macro-averaged normalized Brier score and normalized negative log-likelihood in the main comparison, with relative reductions of 9.5% and 20.2% against the strongest non-CITP baseline for each metric.
Aktxw1WEaI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of turning prompt-induced instability into a learnable refinement signal interesting, and consider controlled comparisons such as the shuffled-contrast control convincing.
Aktxw1WEaI.main_concern: Methodological novelty is thin, since the point predictor reduces to signed affine logit pooling with a Laplace approximation and most of the gain over pooling baselines comes from scale and bias terms.

mAQpRHTwMb.one_liner: Sampling from the clean prediction plus self-correction training lets continuous diffusion solve globally constrained discrete tasks like Sudoku.
mAQpRHTwMb.problem: Standard DDPM sampling stays close to the current noisy state, so early discrete errors in constrained tasks such as Sudoku, graph connectivity, Latin squares and N-queens are hard to undo.
mAQpRHTwMb.method: At inference they sample directly from the model's clean prediction instead of standard samplers, without retraining (a Tweedie reprojection per the reviews). They also add self-correction training that exposes the model to its own predictions to reduce train-test mismatch.
mAQpRHTwMb.key_idea: Re-project from the denoiser's clean prediction at each step instead of staying near the noisy state, and train the denoiser on its own prediction errors.
mAQpRHTwMb.evidence: Sudoku, graph connectivity, Latin squares and N-queens, comparing standard samplers with clean-prediction sampling, with and without self-correction training.
mAQpRHTwMb.claimed_gains: Without retraining, sampling directly from the clean prediction improves Sudoku validity from 31% to 95%, with consistent gains across the other discrete tasks.
mAQpRHTwMb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written, the clean-prediction sampling simple and effective, and the self-correction loss useful for improving other samplers.
mAQpRHTwMb.main_concern: Motivation and novelty are questioned, since discrete diffusion or LLMs fit these tasks more naturally and both components resemble DDIM-style updates and prior scheduled-sampling methods.

h9ltDKMv4s.one_liner: Builds DAG box embeddings without training, choosing each dimension as a witness separating declared pairs, with a machine-checkable certificate.
h9ltDKMv4s.problem: Trained taxonomy embeddings leave residual containment errors and let corpus frequencies shape their geometry.
h9ltDKMv4s.method: The method builds on GRAIL, a reachability index that labels each DAG node with one interval per random linear extension, and lifts it into box space. Instead of random extensions, each dimension is selected as a witness separating specific pairs from a declared disjointness family, giving certified zero containment and separation violations on that family.
h9ltDKMv4s.key_idea: Pick each box dimension as a witness that separates specific declared-disjoint pairs rather than a random linear extension, giving a violation-free geometry by construction.
h9ltDKMv4s.evidence: Gene Ontology, MeSH and WordNet, comparing against randomised GRAIL labels and gradient-trained box baselines on violations and on retrieval ranking by box volume.
h9ltDKMv4s.claimed_gains: Certified zero containment and separation violations on the declared family, whereas randomised GRAIL labels still violate it at four times the dimension budget and gradient-trained box baselines leave residual violations; construction takes seconds.
h9ltDKMv4s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the compact representation with formal correctness proofs and machine-verifiable certificates, and the clear separation between always-guaranteed containment and user-chosen separation.
h9ltDKMv4s.main_concern: The certificate covers only a pre-specified separation family rather than all incomparable pairs, and the downstream benefit of the chosen dimensions is not isolated from random-order baselines.

9QR0Pmd4It.one_liner: Averages internal representations over all 24 option permutations of the model's chosen answer before error detection.
9QR0Pmd4It.problem: Internal-state error judgments vary when the same semantic answer is expressed under different answer frames, entangling answer identity with correctness.
9QR0Pmd4It.method: AFS fixes the model-selected semantic answer, teacher-forces its mapped label under all 24 option permutations of a four-option multiple-choice question, and averages the resulting internal representations, which makes the average invariant to the initial answer frame, before a detector such as VIB-Probe is applied.
9QR0Pmd4It.key_idea: Averaging teacher-forced representations over all option permutations suppresses answer-label information so detectors read the correctness signal instead.
9QR0Pmd4It.evidence: 6,400 rule-generated visual questions across 16 reasoning types, 11 detectors, four Qwen3.5 model sizes, in-domain and out-of-domain settings, plus four model families and GPQA Diamond.
9QR0Pmd4It.claimed_gains: AFS + VIB-Probe reaches a mean Macro-F1 of 71.38% versus 63.52% for the strongest baseline selected separately in each setting (+7.85 pp), leading in seven of eight model-domain settings.
9QR0Pmd4It.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation of separating answer identity from correctness is meaningful, the method is simple and detector-agnostic, and the experimental evaluation is extensive.
9QR0Pmd4It.main_concern: The method applies only to multiple-choice questions, needs 24 permutation passes (high inference cost), and its novelty over work on answer-order bias is unclear.

NCOzhCyGPt.one_liner: Detector-aware neural attenuation field with area-based pixel ray aggregation, shared monotone beam-hardening response, and a coarse detector-plane intensity correction.
NCOzhCyGPt.problem: Sparse-view CBCT neural attenuation fields model each detector pixel as one center ray and use weakly constrained spectral and low-frequency terms, so mismatches get absorbed into the attenuation field and distort anatomy.
NCOzhCyGPt.method: Coherent Aperture Aggregation samples multiple physically realizable paths over each area-based detector pixel and averages transmitted intensities; Material-Coupled Response replaces a free voxel-wise beam-hardening spread with a compact, globally shared monotone function of attenuation; and a coarse non-negative detector-plane intensity field corrects additive photon flux as a nuisance term.
NCOzhCyGPt.key_idea: Structure the nuisance degrees of freedom at the measurement level: multi-ray detector area integration, a shared attenuation-to-spread response, and a low-bandwidth additive intensity field.
NCOzhCyGPt.evidence: Two real anthropomorphic phantom datasets spanning three anatomies and multiple sparse-view settings, with perceptual and vascular metrics, ablations, GH-NAF comparisons, held-out projections, and cupping analysis.
NCOzhCyGPt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the detector-measurement mismatch is a real problem motivated by correct physics, and that evaluation on two real phantom datasets is a strength.
NCOzhCyGPt.main_concern: Novelty is incremental (multi-ray area sampling and the spectral formula come from earlier CT and NeRF work), attenuation accuracy is not directly established, the ablation shows little benefit from aperture aggregation, and reconstruction speed is not reported.

96JvRJtabx.one_liner: A causal-Transformer critic values every chunk prefix in one pass, letting offline-to-online RL pick action chunk length per state.
96JvRJtabx.problem: Chunked RL methods use a fixed chunk length, but the best length varies across states and tasks.
96JvRJtabx.method: ACH estimates action-values for all candidate chunk lengths at once with a causal Transformer value function and selects the length adaptively from those values, during both training and inference. Reviewers describe policy extraction with DDPG plus behavior cloning and a Boltzmann distribution over lengths.
96JvRJtabx.key_idea: Action-values of all prefixes of a candidate chunk are estimated in a single causal-Transformer pass, and chunk length is chosen by comparing those values at each state.
96JvRJtabx.evidence: 34 tasks including OGBench and robomimic (10 seeds with confidence intervals per reviews) against fixed-length baselines such as QC, and VLA experiments on two SimplerEnv embodiments with four seeds.
96JvRJtabx.claimed_gains: Outperforms fixed-length baselines in most of 34 tasks and improves VLA models; magnitudes are not stated in the abstract.
96JvRJtabx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and clearly motivated, fits existing chunked RL, and shows broad benchmark coverage with gains over the fixed-length backbone on long-horizon manipulation and in VLA settings.
96JvRJtabx.main_concern: Comparison with the strongest chunked baselines is limited (best-of-N QC and SEAR), the method depends on critic ranking quality without calibration analysis, and there is no theoretical account, physical-robot validation, or inference latency report.

VjdJ253Q5f.one_liner: Audio gradient inversion that constrains reconstruction with a learned mel-spectrogram GAN prior and a neural vocoder, trained on identity-disjoint speakers.
VjdJ253Q5f.problem: Existing audio gradient inversion attacks mostly reconstruct inputs directly in feature space and have been studied under relatively favourable settings, leaving leakage under perturbed gradients less understood.
VjdJ253Q5f.method: Reconstruction is constrained with a learnt mel-spectrogram generative prior and waveforms are recovered with a neural vocoder, with the generator trained on an identity-disjoint speaker split to prevent memorisation of victim identities.
VjdJ253Q5f.key_idea: Optimize in the latent space of a mel-spectrogram generator trained on disjoint speakers, then vocode the result, so the prior adds information when gradients are noisy or compressed.
VjdJ253Q5f.evidence: Speech Commands V2 and AudioMNIST under gradient clipping with Gaussian perturbation, compressed MFCC features, trained victim models and different architectures.
VjdJ253Q5f.claimed_gains: At the strongest perturbation (z=10^-3), where the GAN-free baseline drops to 18.0% and 29.3%, speaker recovery remains at 84.0% on AudioMNIST and 96.5% on Speech Commands.
VjdJ253Q5f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the evaluation fairly comprehensive with useful controls (speaker-disjoint split, perturbations, MFCC compression) and substantial gains under perturbed gradients.
VjdJ253Q5f.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited because the framework largely inherits GIFD from the image domain, with little analysis of failures such as poor results on ResNet18 and AST.

PfWQktVdYn.one_liner: A masked discrete diffusion LLM predicts coarse 3D poses from images and text, then a continuous diffusion prior refines them.
PfWQktVdYn.problem: Autoregressive models struggle to preserve coupled joint constraints under causal decoding, while continuous pose diffusion priors give plausible geometry but lack language grounding.
PfWQktVdYn.method: PoseDLLM splits pose prediction into two stages: a dLLM with bidirectional attention and parallel denoising handles multimodal conditions across tasks, then a continuous diffusion prior refines the coarse prediction toward the biomechanically plausible pose manifold via test-time optimization.
PfWQktVdYn.key_idea: Use a masked discrete diffusion LLM as the semantic engine for multimodal conditions, then refine its coarse pose with a continuous diffusion prior at test time.
PfWQktVdYn.evidence: Human3.6M, PoseScript, PoseFix, and Posepart benchmarks across task configurations, compared with autoregressive LLM baselines.
PfWQktVdYn.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms autoregressive LLM baselines across all task configurations; no numbers in the abstract.
PfWQktVdYn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coarse-to-fine split between discrete semantic reasoning and continuous geometric refinement is coherent, and results are strong across several pose tasks and input modalities.
PfWQktVdYn.main_concern: The link from diffusion-based language generation to better pose reasoning is weakly supported (the pose is regressed from one hidden state), gains are confounded with the stronger LLaDA-V backbone, and the projection interpretation of the prior is unsupported.

ObCJSQGv4o.one_liner: Black-box audit of LLM APIs using stable factual recall near the knowledge boundary as a model fingerprint.
ObCJSQGv4o.problem: Users of relay and reseller APIs cannot directly verify which model actually serves their requests, so model substitution goes undetected.
ObCJSQGv4o.method: KBF generates benign, renewable probes of stable factual recall near the knowledge boundary, including repeatable wrong answers, and calibrates audit decisions against the reference endpoint's self-variation.
ObCJSQGv4o.key_idea: Fingerprint a model by its repeatable correct and incorrect answers on facts near its knowledge boundary, then test a relay's answers against the official endpoint's self-variation.
ObCJSQGv4o.evidence: 16 production endpoints with 155 substitutions and 16 same-reference controls, mixed-routing simulations, and field audits of 28 endpoints across six platforms.
ObCJSQGv4o.claimed_gains: Detects all 155 economically relevant substitutions without rejecting any of the 16 same-reference controls, reaches 95% TPR at a substitution rate as low as 15% in mixed routing, flags 7 of 28 field endpoints, and costs about $0.67 per online audit after enrollment.
ObCJSQGv4o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that verifying relay APIs is practically important and that using stable factual recall as a black-box fingerprint is an interesting, low-cost approach with thorough experiments.
ObCJSQGv4o.main_concern: Adaptive providers that recognize audit probes and route them to the correct model are not evaluated, and dependence between probes may weaken the false-positive guarantees.

pG6Hh28HWr.one_liner: IMTS forecaster that allocates a fixed patch budget by sampling density and retrieves query-conditioned evidence over multi-scale supports.
pG6Hh28HWr.problem: Patch-based irregular multivariate time series methods ignore cross-variable sampling heterogeneity when partitioning, and build multi-scale views before the target variable-time query identifies the relevant history.
pG6Hh28HWr.method: SPAQR distributes a fixed per-sample patch budget across variables and temporal splits by observation density, temporal span, and internal gaps, and encodes each fixed support at coarse, boundary, and transition scales. Each forecast query then softly weights supports and their internal states via evidence retrieval without changing the partition.
pG6Hh28HWr.key_idea: Allocates patches per variable by observation density, temporal span, and gaps, then lets each target variable-time query reweight multi-scale supports without changing the partition.
pG6Hh28HWr.evidence: Four public IMTS benchmarks against sixteen baselines under a common protocol, with ablations and sensitivity studies.
pG6Hh28HWr.claimed_gains: Achieves the lowest mean MSE and MAE on every dataset across four benchmarks and sixteen baselines; no numeric margins stated.
pG6Hh28HWr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find sampling-aware patch allocation well motivated and the comparison across four datasets and sixteen baselines comprehensive.
pG6Hh28HWr.main_concern: Methodological justification is thin: variable-length patch allocation lacks theory (versus fixed-time-length patching in PrimeNet and ReIMTS), the score weights are unablated, and strong baselines such as HyperIMTS are missing.

Mw3lXYlgYU.one_liner: Context distillation that segments agent trajectories into stages and upsamples training steps from the bottleneck stage few episodes reach.
Mw3lXYlgYU.problem: Environment-free learning from logged agent trajectories works on some benchmarks but not others, because a weak deployed agent rarely reaches later task stages, leaving few training steps there.
Mw3lXYlgYU.method: CDUP has an LM agent segment trajectories into task stages, identifies the bottleneck as the first stage few episodes reach, and upsamples steps from it when training with context distillation. In context distillation the teacher is the same model conditioned on experience summarized from the trajectories.
Mw3lXYlgYU.key_idea: Upsamples training steps from the first task stage few logged episodes reach, so context-distillation teacher targets cover decisions the weak deployed agent rarely visits.
Mw3lXYlgYU.evidence: WebShop and ScienceWorld (ALFWorld also introduced) with 3B models (Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-3B), compared with CD and OPCD using budget-matched controls such as random-state, loss-weighting, and balanced-sampling.
Mw3lXYlgYU.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract describes a simple and effective recipe without numbers.
Mw3lXYlgYU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the bottleneck diagnosis is clear and meaningful and the budget-matched comparisons between CD and CDUP make the result trustworthy.
Mw3lXYlgYU.main_concern: Evidence is limited in scale and robustness: only 3B models, a single training seed, and heavy dependence on a strong external LLM for stage segmentation and guidance.

xpeuy3Ebeb.one_liner: Shows weak transfer of shadow-trained attribute classifiers can coexist with strong target-side decodability, using orthogonal alignment and invertible rotation controls.
xpeuy3Ebeb.problem: Attribute-inference audits of graph LLMs judge decodability by transferring shadow-model classifiers to target representations, but it is unclear whether low transfer means low target-side decodability.
xpeuy3Ebeb.method: Orthogonal alignment adjusts the coordinate directions of shadow representations to match target representations while preserving attribute information. Invertible rotation changes only the coordinate directions of target representations without removing information, with a classifier retrained on target representations as the reference.
xpeuy3Ebeb.key_idea: Control coordinates, not information: orthogonal alignment recovers transfer, while invertible rotation of target representations breaks transfer and leaves retrained linear classifiers nearly unchanged.
xpeuy3Ebeb.evidence: Controlled experiments on graph-language models with two molecular datasets, multiple seeds, two decoder models, and matched-training and structure-based splits.
xpeuy3Ebeb.claimed_gains: Alignment improves transfer by up to approximately 0.30 macro AUROC, and invertible rotation reduces shadow-classifier transfer by approximately 0.16 macro AUROC while a retrained linear classifier is nearly unchanged.
xpeuy3Ebeb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experiments are well controlled with clear comparisons, and that the distinction between a failed transferred probe and low target-side decodability is useful for privacy audits.
xpeuy3Ebeb.main_concern: The finding is seen as unsurprising (separately trained networks do not align), the threat model and sensitivity of the attributes are questionable, and coverage is limited to two datasets and two models.

QjUQar53dr.one_liner: ECR revises long-video answers only when a structured certificate shows challenger support, anchor refutation, and admissible evidence.
QjUQar53dr.problem: Evidence supporting an alternative answer does not necessarily refute the current one, so long-video agents lack a principled rule for when new evidence justifies revising an answer.
QjUQar53dr.method: Training-free post-answer revision: the current answer is the anchor and a new answer is the challenger; challenger support, anchor refutation, and evidence admissibility are judged separately and recorded in a certificate. A fixed reason-conditioned policy then retains the anchor, switches, or escalates residual conflicts to blind pairwise arbitration.
QjUQar53dr.key_idea: Separate challenger support from anchor refutation and evidence admissibility in a certificate, and apply a fixed reason-conditioned policy to keep, switch, or arbitrate.
QjUQar53dr.evidence: Video-MME Long with a frozen AVP agent, a 655-question exact-replay cohort with frozen proposals, and a compute-matched symmetric selector comparison with ablations.
QjUQar53dr.claimed_gains: Raises a frozen AVP agent from 52.11% to 62.33% on Video-MME Long while preserving 94.9% of initially correct answers; in replay it reaches 65.50% accuracy with 99 fixes and 13 breaks versus 65.19%, 141 fixes, and 57 breaks for unguarded adoption; ECR-K2 reaches 55.29% versus 52.16% for a compute-matched symmetric selector.
QjUQar53dr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the support-versus-refutation reframing is sensible and that ECR substantially reduces harmful revisions (breaks) while keeping accuracy close to unconditional challenger adoption.
QjUQar53dr.main_concern: The causal benefit is not statistically established (ECR-K2 against the matched symmetric selector has McNemar p = 0.1849 and an interval including zero), and the LLM-based certificate judgments are not validated.

s5U1faMhmf.one_liner: Data-free model merging that learns task-specific input gates on each task vector to preserve own-task inputs and suppress others.
s5U1faMhmf.problem: Merging methods manipulate task vectors but not the input representations they act on, so after merging each task vector may operate on other tasks' inputs and cause cross-task interference.
s5U1faMhmf.method: GTA builds a gated task vector (task vector times a gate G_t) and performs task arithmetic over the gated vectors. G_t is a PSI-Gate designed to preserve input representations of its own task and suppress those of other tasks, and it is learned without the original training data.
s5U1faMhmf.key_idea: Multiply each task vector by a learned input-side gate that keeps its own task's input representations and suppresses other tasks', estimated from task-vector-derived surrogates.
s5U1faMhmf.evidence: Nested 8/14/20-task vision settings, LLaMA at three sizes, Qwen2-7B, and generative reasoning tasks per reviews, compared with baselines such as ACTMat, TSV, and WUDI.
s5U1faMhmf.claimed_gains: Improves task-performance recovery by over 16 percentage points across vision and language models (stated in the TL;DR).
s5U1faMhmf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the input-side view of interference is clear and useful, the evaluation is broad with mechanism-level validation, and the gates add no inference cost.
s5U1faMhmf.main_concern: The SGD-based theory (whose limit equals ACTMat) does not match the optimizers used in experiments, and gains over ACTMat on language tasks are marginal.

A5vFbwU8uS.one_liner: REPAIR-OPD applies local teacher corrections, regenerates student continuations, and trains only on outcome-verified wrong-to-correct repairs.
A5vFbwU8uS.problem: Token-level on-policy distillation corrections do not guarantee better final outcomes because they can redirect the entire autoregressive continuation.
A5vFbwU8uS.method: REPAIR-OPD identifies candidate repair points from teacher confidence and teacher-student disagreement, applies a local teacher correction, and lets the student regenerate the rest of the trajectory. Only Judge-verified wrong-to-correct repairs are used for learning.
A5vFbwU8uS.key_idea: Insert a teacher token correction at a disagreement point, let the student regenerate the suffix, and keep only repairs a judge verifies as wrong-to-correct.
A5vFbwU8uS.evidence: Five mathematical-reasoning and two out-of-domain benchmarks, smaller Qwen and cross-family Llama settings, a matched one-round efficiency test on 1,000 source questions, and a matched-seed comparison.
A5vFbwU8uS.claimed_gains: Overall mean of 54.55%, 4.72% above the strongest OPD baseline, at 1.36x OPD's end-to-end training time and 1.69x its seven-benchmark mean response length.
A5vFbwU8uS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding distillation in final outcomes rather than local token corrections is intuitive and simple to adopt, and that the experiments cover several OPD baselines, model sizes and benchmarks.
