A5vFbwU8uS.main_concern: Ablations and controls do not isolate the repair mechanism: the method adds extra sampling, judge filtering and a different objective, and lacks compute-matched comparisons with simpler outcome-based baselines.

RHTjeFhx9E.one_liner: Transformer with object queries predicts metric scene geometry, 3D tracks and 6D object pose from robot RGB video.
RHTjeFhx9E.problem: No unified geometry foundation model exists for robotic scenes that also recovers object motion and 6D pose.
RHTjeFhx9E.method: Extracts visual tokens from RGB observations, adds object queries with optional prompt tokens, and models them with a spatiotemporal transformer across views and frames. Multiple heads decode camera poses, metric depth, point maps, dense 3D tracks, and object 6D pose, size, oriented box, mask and visibility; training has two stages combining heterogeneous scene-geometry supervision with partially labeled object-state data.
RHTjeFhx9E.key_idea: Object queries and optional prompt tokens join visual tokens in a shared spatiotemporal transformer, with separate heads decoding geometry, motion and object state in one metric reference frame.
RHTjeFhx9E.evidence: Point-map, depth and camera-pose results on six robot-operation datasets, dynamic 3D tracking on four core datasets, object-center and rotation errors, and downstream closed-loop manipulation per reviews.
RHTjeFhx9E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important for robotics and the evaluation is broad, covering geometry, tracking, object state and downstream manipulation, with strong geometry metrics.
RHTjeFhx9E.main_concern: Missing ablations and fairness gaps: EVGT is evaluated in-distribution against zero-shot baselines, object-pose errors are large (for example 123 degrees on DexYCB), and some baselines such as Depth Anything 3 are omitted.

7OM4vVAkEd.one_liner: Weights multiple teachers per token in on-policy distillation using each teacher's displacement from a shared reference model.
7OM4vVAkEd.problem: Domain-routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation needs domain labels and keeps one teacher fixed per response, so it cannot adapt when the required expertise changes within a trajectory.
7OM4vVAkEd.method: At each student-generated prefix, TrustMOPD measures how far each specialist's next-token preferences deviate from the shared reference, calibrates the magnitude across teachers, and uses the scores as local reliability weights on teacher-specific distillation losses.
7OM4vVAkEd.key_idea: A specialist deviates more from its shared reference on in-domain prompts, so per-token displacement in next-token preferences serves as a label-free reliability weight.
7OM4vVAkEd.evidence: Evaluated on mathematics, code and instruction following, trained on SingleCap and MultiCap, with five random seeds per reviews and a theory linking shifts to teacher utility differences.
7OM4vVAkEd.claimed_gains: Closes 91.5% and 98.0% of the overall-score gap between the initial student and oracle-routed teachers on SingleCap and MultiCap, versus 54.4% and 54.5% for the strongest label-free baseline.
7OM4vVAkEd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical, needing no domain labels, router or verifier, and that it beats label-free baselines by about 2 to 2.5 overall points.
7OM4vVAkEd.main_concern: Displacement from the reference is not shown to track local teacher correctness, since a large shift could reflect a preference change or a confident error.

o12hd5fPW8.one_liner: Adds an auxiliary loss that trains uniform-state diffusion language models to retain unperturbed tokens, cutting uncoordinated per-step revisions.
o12hd5fPW8.problem: Uniform-state diffusion models (DUO, UDLM, uniform-noise SEDD) keep revising 173-270 of 512 positions per step because they do not retain correct tokens, which collapses sample diversity.
o12hd5fPW8.method: CTR-Reg is an auxiliary loss that trains the model to retain tokens left unperturbed by the forward process, with no change to the sampler. It follows diagnostics from a random-token corruption experiment and a NELBO decomposition showing training barely rewards retention.
o12hd5fPW8.key_idea: An auxiliary loss penalizes wrong predictions at positions the forward process left clean, which the NELBO barely penalizes.
o12hd5fPW8.evidence: Corruption experiments and a NELBO decomposition diagnose the deficit; CTR-Reg is evaluated on six benchmarks and generative perplexity with greedy-tail decoding, using 0.1B models trained on about 20B tokens per reviews.
o12hd5fPW8.claimed_gains: Clean-token accuracy improves by 26.5 percentage points on average across six benchmarks with corrupted-token accuracy virtually unchanged, and per-step revisions fall to 3-11 positions.
o12hd5fPW8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the retention failure is a concrete, well-diagnosed issue and that CTR-Reg is simple, cheap to train and clearly presented.
o12hd5fPW8.main_concern: Training scale is small (about 20B tokens for 0.1B models versus far more for baselines like DUO), so it is unclear the retention issue persists at normal scale, and simpler alternative objectives are not compared.

9DCi9Y8fYl.one_liner: Matrix sketches retain dominant preference-curvature directions to reduce the cost of online reward-model updates.
9DCi9Y8fYl.problem: Online RLHF estimators can require curvature computations and storage that scale at least quadratically with feature dimension.
9DCi9Y8fYl.method: GeoSRM approximates accumulated preference geometry with matrix sketches instead of maintaining full curvature matrices. The analysis quantifies efficiency–utility trade-offs across deployment and active preference-collection settings.
9DCi9Y8fYl.key_idea: Maintain a sketch of dominant preference-geometry directions in place of the full high-dimensional curvature matrix.
9DCi9Y8fYl.evidence: Theoretical estimation and policy guarantees accompany deployment and active-learning experiments across model sizes and sketch configurations.
9DCi9Y8fYl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard preference-curvature cost as an important bottleneck and value sketching with explicit statistical trade-off analysis.
9DCi9Y8fYl.main_concern: Experimental response selection and optimization settings differ from the analyzed algorithm, leaving the theoretical guarantees' practical applicability unclear.

PlfFyV6wbZ.one_liner: Coupled hard instances and sharper S-GDA analysis characterize deterministic oracle complexity for two-sided Polyak–Łojasiewicz minimax optimization.
PlfFyV6wbZ.problem: Lower and upper complexity bounds for smooth two-sided Polyak–Łojasiewicz minimax problems leave a gap in accuracy dependence.
PlfFyV6wbZ.method: The paper constructs a deterministic first-order oracle lower bound and sharpens the single-loop Smoothed Gradient-Descent-Ascent analysis. It states explicit initialization costs and identifies a high-accuracy subclass where bounds match.
PlfFyV6wbZ.key_idea: Couple primal and dual hard-instance chains and refine S-GDA's Lyapunov analysis to match condition-number dependence under controlled initialization.
PlfFyV6wbZ.evidence: Theoretical results cover jointly smooth objectives satisfying Polyak–Łojasiewicz conditions in both variables, with matching bounds on an initialization-controlled subclass.
PlfFyV6wbZ.claimed_gains: The lower bound is Omega(kappa_x kappa_y log(Delta/epsilon)), and the S-GDA upper bound removes an additional logarithmic factor in target accuracy from previous multi-loop guarantees.
PlfFyV6wbZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the nontrivial lower-bound construction and sharper upper-bound analysis for deterministic minimax optimization.
PlfFyV6wbZ.main_concern: One reviewer questions whether uncontrolled initial dual gaps invalidate a uniform optimal-complexity claim for the broadly defined problem class.

iECbeo2ucE.one_liner: Human-verified egocentric questions measure body configuration, motion dynamics, and temporal reasoning beyond coarse action recognition.
iECbeo2ucE.problem: Existing multimodal evaluations poorly assess body-motion reasoning when egocentric videos only partially reveal the wearer's body.
iECbeo2ucE.method: SOMA organizes fine-grained body-motion questions along three capability axes and evaluates models against human performance. It also provides aligned video, body-motion, and language supervision for a multimodal baseline.
iECbeo2ucE.key_idea: Turn fine-grained egocentric body-motion annotations into human-verified questions with controls against language-only shortcuts.
iECbeo2ucE.evidence: The benchmark contains 1,632 questions and evaluates 37 closed-source, open-source, and specialized egocentric MLLMs alongside humans.
iECbeo2ucE.claimed_gains: Humans reach 68.5% accuracy from video alone, while the strongest zero-shot MLLM, Qwen3.6-27B, reaches 50.0%.
iECbeo2ucE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating fine-grained egocentric body motion and appreciate human verification and shortcut controls.
iECbeo2ucE.main_concern: Occluded or out-of-frame body cues make some questions ambiguous or visually unanswerable, complicating interpretation of model errors.

QTAnJswuMj.one_liner: Supervises adaptive graph propagation controls using loss differences between explicit alternatives, batching distant nodes for exact comparisons.
QTAnJswuMj.problem: Gradients at current propagation settings capture only local sensitivity and cannot directly compare distinct downstream behaviors.
QTAnJswuMj.method: Counterfactual Supervision temporarily sets each selected continuous control to two alternatives and recomputes subsequent layers. Loss differences supplement ordinary optimization, while locality-aware batching evaluates sufficiently distant nodes together without changing individual comparisons.
QTAnJswuMj.key_idea: Paired control interventions produce downstream-loss targets, and independent-set batching preserves exact nodewise comparisons during shared recomputations.
QTAnJswuMj.evidence: Experiments evaluate adaptive propagation on varied node-classification datasets, compare local-gradient preferences with endpoint comparisons, and test transfer to Mowst.
QTAnJswuMj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the concrete motivation for endpoint comparisons and the exact batching construction that reduces their cost.
QTAnJswuMj.main_concern: Missing matched control-only update baselines leave gains from counterfactual targets confounded with additional optimization steps.

Slv0AxrpTv.one_liner: Maps personal knowledge-graph updates into circuit-level activation steering to inject mutable user facts.
Slv0AxrpTv.problem: Private entities produce unstable editing keys, and multi-attribute personal updates can collide under subject-bound knowledge editing.
Slv0AxrpTv.method: SPIKE identifies model components suited to personal knowledge injection and uses a KG-LLM Alignment Module to generate steering activations from structured personal knowledge. Experiments examine updates alongside preservation of existing facts.
Slv0AxrpTv.key_idea: A knowledge-graph alignment module converts personal fact representations into activation interventions at selected language-model components.
Slv0AxrpTv.evidence: Experiments cover several language models, four datasets, editing baselines, multi-attribute updates, and comparisons of attention and feed-forward interventions.
Slv0AxrpTv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize personal fact updating as a practical problem distinct from conventional editing of public knowledge.
Slv0AxrpTv.main_concern: Locality tests derive new steering vectors from unchanged facts instead of keeping actual update vectors active, weakening preservation claims and baseline comparability.

7K1S8y2CXa.one_liner: Conditions model actions on counts of qualifying workflow events and tests whether models learn counting rules or shortcuts.
7K1S8y2CXa.problem: High backdoor activation success does not establish that models selectively count intended task-defined units.
7K1S8y2CXa.method: CountTrigger formalizes cardinality predicates and connects them to Transformer expressivity results. Counterfactual tests, finite-state supervision, and causal interventions examine rule acquisition and the influence of internal count representations.
7K1S8y2CXa.key_idea: Selective accumulation of qualifying events defines cardinality triggers, while counterfactual supervision separates intended predicates from shortcut activation strategies.
7K1S8y2CXa.evidence: Across-model and across-task experiments combine counterfactual controls, mixed-type held-out compositions, event-state interventions, and count-direction steering.
7K1S8y2CXa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the distinction between successful trigger activation and learning the intended counting predicate.
7K1S8y2CXa.main_concern: Current interventions and generalization tests do not establish a stable, behaviorally effective selective-counting mechanism.

SM3s5iEIOw.one_liner: Organizes motion-salient frames, object-event evidence, and corrected mask propagation to localize small video anomalies.
SM3s5iEIOw.problem: Small-object anomaly cues can disappear beneath dominant normal backgrounds in complex scenes.
SM3s5iEIOw.method: SAVOR adaptively selects keyframes and consolidates sparse trajectories into persistent events for joint global-local reasoning. Mask feedback retargets unreliable anchors to guide bidirectional SAM2 propagation without in-domain training.
SM3s5iEIOw.key_idea: Motion-aware temporal mosaics and persistent object events organize anomaly evidence, while mask-guided anchor retargeting stabilizes cross-frame propagation.
SM3s5iEIOw.evidence: Experiments evaluate standard video-anomaly benchmarks and the small-object anomaly localization benchmark, with component ablations.
SM3s5iEIOw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that small-object anomalies are an important problem and that the framework shows encouraging localization results.
SM3s5iEIOw.main_concern: Trajectory construction needs clearer specification and validation when anomalous objects lack reliable motion cues.

dZYhKAjTH2.one_liner: Mines reusable action hierarchies from trajectories and incorporates them into agent training through examples, rewards, or teacher context.
dZYhKAjTH2.problem: Flat action-stream training ignores recurring sub-procedures and fails to fully exploit scarce agent trajectories.
dZYhKAjTH2.method: X-Tree scores canonicalized action spans for reuse and merges them into a hierarchy without LLM calls. Tree nodes become offline training instances, online skill bonuses, or privileged self-distillation context.
dZYhKAjTH2.key_idea: Success- and length-aware merging of canonicalized action spans builds a reusable skill hierarchy that supplies structured training signals.
dZYhKAjTH2.evidence: Matched-data and budget experiments cover WebArena, ScienceWorld, and WebShop at three model scales, with random-span, random-tree, and mining-corpus controls.
dZYhKAjTH2.claimed_gains: X-Tree reports gains of up to 4.5% SR on WebArena, 5.8% SR on ScienceWorld, and 4.1% success on WebShop.
dZYhKAjTH2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate deterministic, auditable hierarchy mining and its integration into several training settings.
dZYhKAjTH2.main_concern: The stated WebShop self-distillation gate is constant, making the reported teacher-dependent gradient mechanism unclear.

aY8witQgNu.one_liner: Decomposes scientific repositories into verifiable task types and recursively repairs failed environment candidates for agent training.
aY8witQgNu.problem: Scientific agents lack sufficiently large collections of executable and verifiable training environments.
aY8witQgNu.method: POSEIDON extracts Reproduction, Subflow, Completion, and Correction tasks from scientific repositories. A recursive improvement loop repairs failed candidates to construct the PEARL environment collection.
aY8witQgNu.key_idea: Workflow decomposition generates complementary repository tasks, and recursive repair recovers failed environment candidates.
aY8witQgNu.evidence: PEARL contains 97,659 environments from 7,110 repositories across 10 disciplines; Qwen3.5 9B, 27B, and 35B-A3B evaluations cover six scientific-agent benchmarks.
aY8witQgNu.claimed_gains: POSEIDON extracts nearly 10× as many training environments as a prior approach from the same repository budget.
aY8witQgNu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the scale and disciplinary coverage of PEARL and the human audit of task and evaluator quality.
aY8witQgNu.main_concern: Baseline comparisons differ in teacher strength and training-token volume, preventing clean attribution of gains to environment quality or diversity.

A2ld1Uumeh.one_liner: Orthogonally decomposes task vectors relative to pretrained weights and merges corresponding geometric components independently.
A2ld1Uumeh.problem: Whole-vector merging statistics let one geometric component influence how another component is selected or weighted.
A2ld1Uumeh.method: DiGA uses pretrained weights as a shared geometric reference to split task updates into orthogonal components. It applies merging rules independently within component subspaces and recombines the resulting updates.
A2ld1Uumeh.key_idea: Shared-reference orthogonal decomposition separates task-vector components before independent aggregation and recombination.
A2ld1Uumeh.evidence: Experiments include Llama 3B and 8B and Qwen-VL, controlled whole-update versus separate-component comparisons, and integrations with TIES, DARE, and TSVM.
A2ld1Uumeh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find intra-vector geometric coupling a useful perspective and recognize the controlled analyses of component separation.
A2ld1Uumeh.main_concern: Controlled gains from component separation are small, so larger improvements cannot be attributed entirely to the proposed decoupling.

e4LxYgpY94.one_liner: Turns investment questions into evidence-backed stock scores, then evolves questions and selects factor ensembles using return evaluations.
e4LxYgpY94.problem: Fixed numerical formulas cannot fully express investment judgments whose relevant evidence differs across companies.
e4LxYgpY94.method: An executor agent reads records and performs calculations under shared execution and scoring rules to score stocks against natural-language questions. Return-guided evolution revises the questions, and validation performance selects ensembles from all generations.
e4LxYgpY94.key_idea: Common scoring rules operationalize natural-language investment questions, while return feedback revises candidates and validation ranks ensemble members.
e4LxYgpY94.evidence: Fundamental and technical factor experiments cover CSI300 and Nasdaq-100, including formula comparisons, controlled evidence changes, repeated execution, and chronological holdouts.
e4LxYgpY94.claimed_gains: Selected ensembles achieve higher IC and RankIC than initial ensembles in three of four chronologically held-out settings.
e4LxYgpY94.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate evidence-backed measurement and explicit checks of what scores measure separately from return prediction.
e4LxYgpY94.main_concern: Short held-out evaluations and unreported uncertainty make the reliability of predictive gains difficult to assess.

os0zk5Ctsi.one_liner: Trains an open-weight placement model with geometric verification before reinforcement learning on fully routed power, performance, and area.
os0zk5Ctsi.problem: Proprietary placement agents raise confidentiality and cost concerns, while real circuit data and physical-design evaluations are expensive.
os0zk5Ctsi.method: PlaceReasoner-Pro first learns from verified synthetic floorplans with reasoning annotations. Reinforcement learning then progresses from geometric legality rewards to measured PPA from complete OpenROAD place-and-route runs.
os0zk5Ctsi.key_idea: Progressive rewards first enforce placement legality and then optimize physical-design outcomes measured after full routing.
os0zk5Ctsi.evidence: An 8B vision-language model trains on 10K verified synthetic placements and is evaluated on 16 benchmark tasks against Stage-I training and Claude Opus 4.8 in the same harness.
os0zk5Ctsi.claimed_gains: Stage-I raises overlap-free placement from 78.1% to 90.9%; Stage-II improves TNS on 13 of 16 tasks, with 7 vs. 7 WNS wins and 7 vs. 9 TNS wins against Claude Opus 4.8.
os0zk5Ctsi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the progression from cheap geometric supervision to expensive routed objectives and the practical relevance of a compact open-weight model.
os0zk5Ctsi.main_concern: Comparative timing results lack repeated generations and uncertainty estimates, weakening the claimed parity with frontier models.

2odshXSEu5.one_liner: Greedy MMD selection without replacement separates mixtures by tracking selection-order effects and stopping accuracy.
2odshXSEu5.problem: A reference-matched subset can still leave a poor mixture remainder if earlier selections or stopping size are wrong.
2odshXSEu5.method: The analysis bounds how earlier greedy choices affect subsequent MMD approximation. Under geometric conditions and suitable stopping, it establishes convergence for both the selected subset and the remainder.
2odshXSEu5.key_idea: Greedy MMD minimization selects distinct mixture observations to match a reference component, while stopping determines the size and quality of the remainder.
2odshXSEu5.evidence: Error decompositions and conditional convergence proofs accompany simulations and real-data experiments on mixture separation.
2odshXSEu5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical treatment of without-replacement selection and the distinction between subset fit and remainder quality.
2odshXSEu5.main_concern: The guarantees require restrictive geometry and accurate stopping without establishing that practical stopping rules meet those conditions.

p3zjgnMPG6.one_liner: A flat-jet encoder and structured latent dynamics learn coordinates for trajectory planning and control-input recovery.
p3zjgnMPG6.problem: Accurate observation prediction need not provide the state-input relationships required for control under incomplete observations.
p3zjgnMPG6.method: The model learns a flat-jet representation and structured dynamics without true-flat-coordinate supervision. Planned trajectories in learned flat coordinates translate into physical control inputs.
p3zjgnMPG6.key_idea: Differential-flatness structure links learned latent coordinates and finite-order derivatives to physical-state and control-input recovery.
p3zjgnMPG6.evidence: A sufficient observation-condition result and experiments on analytically tractable and image-based flat systems assess prediction, control, and limited-data behavior.
p3zjgnMPG6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find differential flatness a promising bias for learning representations that support control beyond prediction.
p3zjgnMPG6.main_concern: The guarantees rely on structural knowledge and exact flat-coordinate recovery that the learned representation and input-recovery network do not ensure.

FvvEetTAgF.one_liner: Function-grouped persistent residual streams give detection modules task-specific access while shared modules mix information across groups.
FvvEetTAgF.problem: Detection transformers combine classification and localization evidence in a single shared query state despite differing task requirements.
FvvEetTAgF.method: TaskHC groups Hyper-Connection residual streams by function, reconstructs task-specific working states, and writes task updates back to those groups. Shared modules reconstruct joint states and mix across the bank.
FvvEetTAgF.key_idea: Task-specific reconstruction and writeback restrict access to designated residual groups, while shared operations mix the full stream bank.
FvvEetTAgF.evidence: COCO experiments use DEIM–D-FINE and DEIM–RT-DETRv2 baselines with architectural ablations, sampling analyses, and frozen-state probes.
FvvEetTAgF.claimed_gains: For DEIM–D-FINE-L, AP increases from 54.45 to 54.68 with 0.53 ms additional latency on an NVIDIA T4 using TensorRT FP16.
FvvEetTAgF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the motivated state-management mechanism and analyses of functional specialization.
FvvEetTAgF.main_concern: The AP gains are small, and ablation differences lack sufficient repeated-training validation to establish reliable structural conclusions.

97cAXmQ1Zk.one_liner: Point-cloud reconstruction and nominal-view rendering restore camera-shifted VLA inputs, with trajectory-conditioned alignment for asynchronous execution.
97cAXmQ1Zk.problem: Camera shifts can disrupt cross-view coordination, while existing remedies require new paired-view data and VLA fine-tuning.
97cAXmQ1Zk.method: CoRe-VLA reconstructs the scene and renders observations from the training viewpoint without additional multiview collection or VLA fine-tuning. R2C repairs rendering artifacts, and ETCA aligns asynchronous execution with the running trajectory.
97cAXmQ1Zk.key_idea: Reconstructing and re-rendering the scene restores the training viewpoint, while trajectory-conditioned alignment coordinates delayed action updates.
97cAXmQ1Zk.evidence: Experiments cover π0.5, OpenVLA-OFT, and GR00T under camera displacement, plus LIBERO-100, LIBERO-Plus, and real-robot evaluation.
97cAXmQ1Zk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful viewpoint-robustness gains and a motivated combination of view restoration with asynchronous control.
97cAXmQ1Zk.main_concern: The pipeline assumes known camera transforms and intrinsics without adequately explaining real-world calibration or its adaptation cost.

7PwCln99GU.one_liner: Domain-specific LoRA memories reduce writing interference and use prototype-guided routing to reuse knowledge for lifelong person re-identification.
7PwCln99GU.problem: Large domain shifts cause lifelong person re-identification models to overwrite earlier identity-discriminative representations.
7PwCln99GU.method: RPM writes domain-specific low-rank parameter memories using activation-subspace separation, then freezes them for storage. Prototype-similarity routing composes stored memories for each query without retaining historical images.
7PwCln99GU.key_idea: Write LoRA updates in reduced-overlap activation subspaces, freeze them by domain, and compose them using query-to-prototype similarities.
7PwCln99GU.evidence: Lifelong re-identification experiments include same-ViT-backbone comparisons, component and routing ablations, and ten-seed results reported in the appendix.
7PwCln99GU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the decomposition into memory writing, storage, and input-dependent retrieval coherent and relevant to exemplar-free lifelong learning.
7PwCln99GU.main_concern: Retention and dataset-wise superiority claims rely partly on estimated forgetting statistics and per-target decompositions rather than raw baseline evaluations.

dYkP8DiIqC.one_liner: Reward-guided LLM reasoning selects compact relational subgraphs to explain associations between knowledge-graph entities.
dYkP8DiIqC.problem: Entity-centric knowledge-graph question answering does not directly explain associations, while abundant trivial subgraphs obscure informative relational answers.
dYkP8DiIqC.method: UniRel combines subgraph retrieval and pruning with an LLM fine-tuned through reinforcement learning. Its reward favors compact, specific subgraphs containing informative relations and low-degree intermediate entities.
dYkP8DiIqC.key_idea: Reward compact subgraphs with specific relations and low-degree intermediate entities when training an LLM to explain entity associations.
dYkP8DiIqC.evidence: Experiments cover seven knowledge graphs and multiple LLM backbones, unseen entities and relations, conventional entity-centric questions, and a human preference evaluation.
dYkP8DiIqC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the relation-centric KGQA setting and regard the combination of subgraph processing and reward-guided reasoning as reasonable.
dYkP8DiIqC.main_concern: Queries constructed from sampled entity pairs and templates lack sufficient justification as representative real-world information needs.

Uh2vvMhjmA.one_liner: Bitwise evidence feedback adjusts diffusion-language-model token distributions to strengthen weak watermark bits during denoising.
Uh2vvMhjmA.problem: Partially masked, non-causal diffusion contexts accumulate uneven evidence across watermark bits, hindering reliable message recovery.
Uh2vvMhjmA.method: BEFMark uses context-aware multi-layer voting to estimate bitwise evidence and candidate tokens' expected contributions. A KL-regularized distribution update prioritizes weakly supported bits while limiting deviation from the base model.
Uh2vvMhjmA.key_idea: Estimate evidence for each watermark bit during denoising and adapt token probabilities toward weak bits under KL regularization.
Uh2vvMhjmA.evidence: Tests on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-v0-Instruct-7B across multiple datasets assess recovery, text-editing robustness, perplexity, and downstream performance, with adaptive-versus-uniform weighting ablations.
Uh2vvMhjmA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adaptive weighting addresses uneven bit evidence and that the uniform-weighting ablation supports its recovery gains.
Uh2vvMhjmA.main_concern: Inconsistent or insufficiently documented baseline settings leave recovery-quality comparisons difficult to assess.

hIlzn5oGaC.one_liner: Enforces safety constraints at test time by sampling behavior-prior actions and refining them via a primal-only reward-or-cost gradient switch.
hIlzn5oGaC.problem: Safe reinforcement learning methods typically bake cost constraints into policy parameters during training and do not re-verify constraints against the cost critic at the specific state visited during deployment.
hIlzn5oGaC.method: Safe Test-time Extraction of Policies (STEP) samples candidate actions from a behavior prior at decision time and refines each candidate using a primal-only gradient switch that follows the reward gradient when estimated cost is below threshold and applies a cost-reduction gradient otherwise. A safety gate evaluates each candidate as a single-step deviation followed by the behavior policy before execution.
hIlzn5oGaC.key_idea: Refines sampled behavior-prior actions at test time using a state-wise primal gradient switch between reward maximization and cost reduction gated by the cost critic.
hIlzn5oGaC.evidence: Evaluated across 28 offline DSRL tasks over 8 seeds and in online fine-tuning on 5 tasks.
hIlzn5oGaC.claimed_gains: On 28 DSRL tasks over 8 seeds, STEP keeps average cost within the budget on 26 tasks and achieves the highest return among within-budget agents on 16 tasks.
hIlzn5oGaC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simplicity and flexibility of enforcing safety constraints directly at decision time without dual variables or policy retraining, supported by broad experiments across 28 DSRL tasks.
hIlzn5oGaC.main_concern: Reviewers note that nearly half of the 28 tasks use zero refinement steps (K=0)—reducing STEP to constrained best-of-N sampling—while task-specific hyperparameter tuning is not clearly separated from evaluation.

sFn69FwjiL.one_liner: Post-trains dense text retrievers with REINFORCE over von Mises-Fisher embedding policies using conditional-mean projection for variance reduction.
sFn69FwjiL.problem: Contrastive training of dense retrieval models optimizes representation similarity surrogates rather than directly optimizing non-differentiable retrieval metrics or downstream task rewards.
sFn69FwjiL.method: RELER treats unit-normalized query and document embeddings as continuous RL actions sampled from von Mises-Fisher (vMF) distributions centered on encoder outputs, updating the encoder via REINFORCE with a leave-one-out baseline (RLOO) using retrieval or downstream rewards. To reduce high-dimensional sampling noise, conditional-mean projection (CMP) projects sampled embeddings onto the subspace spanned by the encoder output and compared candidate embeddings while preserving policy gradient expectations.
sFn69FwjiL.key_idea: Samples unit-sphere query and document embeddings from von Mises-Fisher policies and projects them onto the candidate-spanned subspace via conditional-mean projection for unbiased, low-variance REINFORCE updates.
sFn69FwjiL.evidence: Evaluated by post-training BGE-M3 and Qwen3-Embedding backbones (0.6B and 4B) on the reasoning-intensive BRIGHT benchmark against InfoNCE and LambdaLoss baselines.
sFn69FwjiL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find modeling continuous embeddings as vMF policy actions combined with unbiased subspace projection (CMP) for gradient variance reduction well thought out and mathematically clean.
sFn69FwjiL.main_concern: Reviewers observe that empirical nDCG@10 improvements over standard InfoNCE fine-tuning on Qwen3-Embedding backbones are very small (around 0.4–0.8 points) and uneven across subsets despite added algorithmic complexity.

KRjNhysqyz.one_liner: Decouples global reference-anchored timbre editing from segment-level expressive TTS control via editable codec tokens and boundary KV-cache reconstruction.
KRjNhysqyz.problem: Existing instruction-based text-to-speech systems cannot simultaneously apply explicit attribute edits to a reference speaker's timbre and vary expressive speaking styles across individual text segments without losing acoustic continuity.
KRjNhysqyz.method: EDICT maps a reference voice and structured timbre-edit instructions into a shared edited codec-token representation that anchors speaker identity across all segments. During generation with a frozen TTS backbone, segment-specific natural-language style instructions are injected while the KV cache is rebuilt at each segment boundary—retaining a bounded acoustic history and refreshing the instruction condition.
KRjNhysqyz.key_idea: Anchors global speaker identity with an edited codec-token representation while rebuilding the TTS KV cache at segment boundaries to swap local style instructions and retain bounded acoustic context.
KRjNhysqyz.evidence: Evaluated across two TTS backbones on synthetic and real recordings, measuring target speaker similarity (WavLM SIM-T), attribute editing and preservation, segment transitions, and human listening tests.
KRjNhysqyz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified interface for global relative timbre editing and segment-wise expressive control, as well as the informative ablations validating boundary KV-cache reconstruction over simple truncation.
KRjNhysqyz.main_concern: Reviewers point out that unedited timbre attributes are preserved less reliably than in baseline models, editing and preservation success are not jointly evaluated per sample, and comparisons with closely related voice-editing and KV-swapping baselines are missing.

odltECWrHs.one_liner: Controls open-ended masked diffusion LLM decoding by advancing a fixed-size local horizon of future mask tokens alongside block commitment.
odltECWrHs.problem: Open-ended generation in masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) requires dynamically sizing an unknown output length, and existing methods rely on complex model-derived signals like EOS statistics or confidence.
odltECWrHs.method: Based on the observation that future [MASK] token exposure directly alters current token predictions, MaskHorizon replaces model-based length estimators with a sliding local horizon of future [MASK] positions that advances with block-level decoding progress. Each forward pass computes predictions only up to the local mask horizon while restricting token commitment to the active decoding block.
odltECWrHs.key_idea: Maintains a sliding local horizon of future [MASK] tokens tied to block-level decoding progress while restricting token commitments to the current active block.
odltECWrHs.evidence: Evaluated on LLaDA and Dream diffusion language models across reasoning and code-generation benchmarks including GSM8K, MATH500, and MBPP.
odltECWrHs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling future mask exposure from active-block token commitment is a clean, training-free insight that simplifies variable-length diffusion decoding.
odltECWrHs.main_concern: Reviewers note that main evaluations use only 100 test examples per benchmark without a separate validation split for threshold tuning, and accuracy drops on benchmarks like MATH500 complicate claims of efficiency gains at matched quality.

vCjPg4NkDw.one_liner: Benchmarks end-to-end autonomous driving over 100-second closed-loop 3DGS-and-diffusion rollouts conditioned on explicit standard-definition map routes.
vCjPg4NkDw.problem: Existing closed-loop autonomous driving benchmarks rely on short evaluation horizons that miss long-term consequences and use ambiguous directional commands instead of explicit road-level navigation routes.
vCjPg4NkDw.method: Odyssey reconstructs 100 driving scenarios from 100-second nuPlan logs using 3D Gaussian Splatting paired with single-step diffusion image refinement to reduce rendering artifacts along closed-loop ego trajectories. It replaces directional commands with explicit standard-definition (SD) map routes and evaluates planners—including VLA models—using SD Route Compliance, Pre-Lane Change Score, and an integrated RouteDS metric.
vCjPg4NkDw.key_idea: Combines 100-second 3DGS-reconstructed closed-loop driving rollouts refined by single-step diffusion with explicit standard-definition map route conditioning and route-compliance metrics.
vCjPg4NkDw.evidence: Evaluated across 100 reconstructed 100-second nuPlan scenarios using state-of-the-art end-to-end driving planners and vision-language-action (VLA) models.
vCjPg4NkDw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the focus on 100-second long-horizon closed-loop rollouts with explicit SD-map route guidance and the photorealistic 3DGS-plus-diffusion visual rendering pipeline.
vCjPg4NkDw.main_concern: Reviewers note that 100 scenes offer limited statistical diversity for rare events, frame-wise diffusion refinement lacks temporal consistency checks, and non-ego traffic relies mostly on non-reactive log playback.

pnx9XFlpdr.one_liner: Reduces VLM hallucinations by verifying visual object claims and attempting verified model-generated replacements before falling back to deletion.
pnx9XFlpdr.problem: Filtering out hallucinated claims in vision-language model outputs reduces error rates but discards visual information that could be preserved by substituting the correct object.
pnx9XFlpdr.method: Model-Substitution Risk Control (MSRC) is a training-free pipeline that verifies visual object claims in VLM outputs and prompts the frozen VLM to propose replacement objects for failed claims. Proposed replacements must pass admissibility rules and independent visual verification calibrated on held-out data to be accepted; otherwise, the unsupported claim is deleted, with risk evaluated against the original pool of claim opportunities.
pnx9XFlpdr.key_idea: Attempts to repair failed visual object claims using frozen-model replacement proposals gated by calibrated visual verification thresholds before defaulting to claim deletion.
pnx9XFlpdr.evidence: Evaluated across image captioning, visual question answering, and hallucination benchmarks including POPE, MME, HaloQuest, and MMHal-Bench against verification-only filtering.
pnx9XFlpdr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that attempting verified repair before deletion is well motivated and praise evaluating hallucination risk over a fixed denominator of original claim opportunities alongside true-claim yield.
pnx9XFlpdr.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the method only extracts and replaces object nouns—leaving unclear how it produces large gains on yes/no, attribute, and counting benchmarks—and note examples where sentence edits exceed the stated span-substitution rule.

0dctX9qW2j.one_liner: Adapts frozen vision-language-action policies to follow negated manipulation instructions via lightweight negation transformation layers and teacher-guided visual token alignment.
0dctX9qW2j.problem: Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models trained on affirmative demonstrations frequently fail to respect explicit negative constraints specifying what the robot must not do.
0dctX9qW2j.method: NegaAlign inserts lightweight trainable Negation Transformation Layers into a frozen VLA backbone to reshape intermediate instruction representations while keeping all pretrained backbone and action-generator weights fixed. During training on image-language supervision derived from existing demonstrations, a teacher-guided alignment objective aligns instruction-relevant visual tokens under negated prompts with those of constraint-satisfying affirmative prompts.
0dctX9qW2j.key_idea: Inserts trainable negation transformation layers into a frozen VLA backbone and aligns visual tokens of negated instructions with constraint-satisfying affirmative teacher representations using image-language supervision.
0dctX9qW2j.evidence: Evaluated on the newly introduced NegaBench simulation benchmark (10 scenarios across 5 domains) and real-robot tasks across GR00T, pi_0, and pi_0.5 backbones.
0dctX9qW2j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that failure on negated instructions is a concrete, practical limitation of current VLAs and appreciate that NegaAlign achieves large gains using parameter-efficient image-language adaptation without negated action trajectories.
0dctX9qW2j.main_concern: Reviewers note that evaluation uses the same small set of manually constructed negated instructions seen during post-training—leaving generalization to unseen negations untested—and lacks a simple rule-based or supervised instruction-rewriting baseline given the same relational supervision.

YmMg6gdHYq.one_liner: Dynamically constructs sparse hypergraphs layer-by-layer using separate controllers for local candidate hyperedge cardinality and global hyperedge count.
YmMg6gdHYq.problem: Dynamic hypergraph neural networks typically use fixed hyperedge counts or fixed cardinality limits, resulting in redundant, oversized, or fragmented hyperedges when relational structures vary across layers and datasets.
YmMg6gdHYq.method: AD-DHGNN generates posterior-weighted candidate hyperedges from anchor-based node similarities and applies a dual control mechanism at each layer: a cardinality controller assigns data-dependent node-capacity budgets to individual candidates, and a count controller selects a compact subset of hyperedges using spectral and coverage criteria. The resulting sparse dynamic hypergraph is used for gated message passing.
YmMg6gdHYq.key_idea: Separately regulates per-hyperedge node cardinality via posterior mixture weights and total hyperedge count via spectral and coverage knee selection before gated hypergraph message passing.
YmMg6gdHYq.evidence: Evaluated on seven node-classification benchmarks including Cora alongside structural redundancy and ablation analyses.
YmMg6gdHYq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing dynamic hypergraph structure learning into local hyperedge cardinality control and global hyperedge count selection is conceptually clear and well motivated.
YmMg6gdHYq.main_concern: Reviewers find the spectral and coverage knee count controller heuristic and brittle to small overlaps between large hyperedges, with limited methodological novelty beyond combining established mixture modeling and spectral rules.

bE0iNWebBO.one_liner: Approximates Brockett-Wegner Hamiltonian operator flows for quantum ground-energy estimation using autoregressive Pauli-string sampling and quadratic coefficient projection.
bE0iNWebBO.problem: Estimating quantum ground-state energies faces exponential growth in the operator basis for operator-flow methods and strong ansatz dependence for wavefunction-based methods.
bE0iNWebBO.method: Neural Quantum Operator Flow (NQOF) reformulates ground-energy optimization as learning a Brockett-Wegner double-bracket flow on the Hamiltonian operator manifold. At each step, an autoregressive neural network samples a compact subset of Pauli strings without enumerating the full basis, and a convex quadratic projection determines their coefficients to approximate the energy-lowering unitary flow direction.
bE0iNWebBO.key_idea: Samples sparse Pauli operator generators with an autoregressive neural network and fits their coefficients via quadratic projection to approximate isospectral Brockett-Wegner energy-lowering flows.
bE0iNWebBO.evidence: Evaluated on molecular and quantum many-body systems with up to 30 qubits, accompanied by truncation-error bounds and flow-fidelity experiments.
bE0iNWebBO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the combination of autoregressive Pauli-string selection and quadratic coefficient fitting to approximate isospectral double-bracket flows clean, well presented, and effective on molecular benchmarks.
bE0iNWebBO.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the state-projected objective closely mirrors Quantum Imaginary Time Evolution (QITE), lacks ablations comparing the learned sampler against greedy or random Pauli selection, and still scales as n^8 (~10^9 Pauli terms at 30 qubits).

WHHqkNG8Yn.one_liner: Traces and mitigates bias in multimodal LLM recommenders via causal chain influence across training samples, SAE concepts, and outcomes.
WHHqkNG8Yn.problem: Multimodal LLM-based recommender systems inherit and amplify biases across modalities and user attributes, but lack mechanisms to attribute outcome biases to specific training samples and mitigate them without costly full retraining.
WHHqkNG8Yn.method: TRACE models bias propagation across three levels—training samples, modality-specific sparse-autoencoder (SAE) concepts, and recommendation outcomes—connected via a causally mediated chain influence score. Using this chain influence, TRACE applies closed-form, one-step LoRA parameter updates via a removal operator that suppresses bias-driving samples, a corrective operator that reinforces preference signals from corrective pairs, and a composed operator integrating both.
WHHqkNG8Yn.key_idea: Computes a three-level causal chain influence linking training samples, identifiable sparse-autoencoder concepts, and recommendation bias to drive closed-form one-step LoRA debiasing operators.
WHHqkNG8Yn.evidence: Evaluated on multimodal recommendation benchmarks including MovieLens across popularity, user-attribute, co-existing, and modality-dominance bias settings.
WHHqkNG8Yn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unified three-level framework connecting training samples, interpretable multimodal concepts, and multiple recommendation bias types with retraining-free closed-form LoRA updates.
WHHqkNG8Yn.main_concern: Reviewers note that sample-level influence attribution via damped diagonal Fisher approximations is never directly validated against true leave-one-out retraining effects, and the causal structural equations rely on strong, unverified assumptions.

4lO5hwlnWC.one_liner: Perturbs RL training rewards with TD-error-directed positive and negative noise to prevent premature convergence to early suboptimal rewards.
4lO5hwlnWC.problem: Deep reinforcement learning agents often get trapped around early rewarding states, while undirected random noise lacks directional control and intrinsic reward models add computational and architectural overhead.
4lO5hwlnWC.method: Bidirectional Reward Noise (BiRN) directly perturbs training rewards using available TD errors and batch bootstrap targets without auxiliary models. It injects negative reward noise to dampen attraction toward dominant early rewarding transitions and positive reward noise to boost transitions exhibiting positive learning potential.
4lO5hwlnWC.key_idea: Injects directionally controlled positive or negative noise directly into training rewards based on transition TD errors and batch-average bootstrap targets.
4lO5hwlnWC.evidence: Evaluated across gridworld, Atari (including Gravitar), IsaacGym, MiniGrid (including Empty-25x25), and cooperative multi-agent matrix games.
4lO5hwlnWC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that BiRN is lightweight, adds negligible runtime overhead (~1.13%), requires no extra networks, and achieves strong gains on several sparse-reward and multi-agent tasks.
4lO5hwlnWC.main_concern: Reviewers point out that BiRN's expected effect is a non-zero deterministic shift of positive-TD targets toward the batch mean—which is never ablated against a deterministic shift without noise—and note that in strictly zero-reward sparse environments before the first goal is reached, zero TD errors would produce no perturbation.

tnvhgIUFEW.one_liner: Distills structure-invariant prototypes and filters unlabeled historical neighbors for graph continual learning under history-aware restricted observability.
tnvhgIUFEW.problem: Fidelity-focused graph condensation in continual learning overfits task-specific spurious structural motifs, while connections between current nodes and unlabeled historical neighbors introduce cross-task neighborhood mixing.
tnvhgIUFEW.method: The authors formalize history-aware restricted observability—where current nodes connect to locally observable, unlabeled historical neighbors—and propose Invariant Structure Distillation for Graph Condensation (ISD-GC). ISD-GC selectively filters historical neighborhood context and distills multi-view structure-invariant prototypes into the replay memory buffer rather than optimizing for raw structural snapshot fidelity.
tnvhgIUFEW.key_idea: Filters unlabeled one-hop historical neighbors and distills multi-view structure-invariant prototypes into a condensed replay buffer to prevent consolidating spurious task-specific graph motifs.
tnvhgIUFEW.evidence: Evaluated on a synthetic Motif Trap diagnostic and four standard graph continual learning datasets (including Reddit) under two observation protocols.
tnvhgIUFEW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the realistic history-aware restricted observability setting where new nodes connect to unlabeled historical nodes and the Motif Trap diagnostic illustrating spurious structural shortcut consolidation.
tnvhgIUFEW.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about poor figure readability, weak empirical isolation of the proposed invariance stages in ablations, and evaluation discrepancies such as using ground-truth task indices at test time.

ipFV10VIUy.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM agents across models and execution harnesses under controlled ambiguity and missingness in goals, context, and constraints.
ipFV10VIUy.problem: How language-model agents respond to ambiguous or missing task specifications across different model backbones and execution harnesses remains poorly characterized.
ipFV10VIUy.method: AM-Bench adapts 48 tasks from Terminal-Bench 2.0 and Harness-Bench, pairing each fully specified reference task with six controlled variants containing ambiguous or missing goals, context, or constraints. The authors evaluate all pairings of five models and four execution harnesses across 20,160 runs, measuring task completion, constraint compliance, token consumption, repeat consistency, and estimated clarification recovery.
ipFV10VIUy.key_idea: Evaluates a full factorial cross of LLM backbones and agent harnesses on matched tasks perturbed with six controlled conditions of ambiguous or missing goals, context, and constraints.
ipFV10VIUy.evidence: Evaluated across 48 base tasks (7 conditions each) over all pairings of 5 models and 4 harnesses totaling 20,160 execution runs.
ipFV10VIUy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled same-task comparison across information conditions, the separation of task completion from constraint compliance, and the joint model-by-harness evaluation design.
ipFV10VIUy.main_concern: Reviewers point out that evaluating underspecified task variants against the single original reference verifier penalizes valid alternative interpretations, and replacing clarification requests with offline fully specified success rates rather than interactive answers overestimates clarification gains.

ZdD1v5tXJG.one_liner: Optimizes subgroup-fair and marginal-fair clustering via a continuous relaxation of an exact covariance-based fairness-gap surrogate.
ZdD1v5tXJG.problem: Enforcing fair clustering across intersectional subgroups defined by multiple sensitive attributes becomes computationally expensive and numerically unstable as the number of subgroups grows exponentially and rare subgroups emerge.
ZdD1v5tXJG.method: The authors define a subgroup-fairness gap for clustering, prove that a covariance-based surrogate exactly matches this gap on discrete assignments, and introduce a continuous relaxation optimized via gradient-based block alternating updates (Cova-FC) with a first-order stationarity guarantee. They further extend the penalty to bound higher-order subgroup-marginal fairness gaps.
ZdD1v5tXJG.key_idea: Replaces combinatorial intersectional subgroup-fairness constraints with an exact covariance-induced fairness gap surrogate and optimizes its continuous relaxation via proximal-gradient updates.
ZdD1v5tXJG.evidence: Supported by equivalence and first-order stationarity proofs and evaluated on fair clustering benchmark datasets across subgroup and higher-order marginal fairness settings.
ZdD1v5tXJG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper is clearly written and that the exact covariance-based reformulation provides a clean, computationally efficient continuous optimization framework for intersectional subgroup-fair clustering.
ZdD1v5tXJG.main_concern: Reviewers note that weighting the fairness gap by subgroup proportions downweights the very rare subgroups motivating the work, and the continuous stationarity guarantee does not carry over to the final discretized cluster assignments.

yTDcIt9mFZ.one_liner: Analyzes weak-to-strong generalization in two-layer ReLU networks when a weak teacher has full easy-feature and partial hard-feature knowledge.
yTDcIt9mFZ.problem: Existing theoretical analyses of weak-to-strong generalization rarely model how a strong student learns when a weak teacher reliably labels easy features but produces stochastic label errors on hard features.
yTDcIt9mFZ.method: The authors analyze gradient-descent training of a two-layer ReLU student network supervised by a weak teacher with complete easy-feature knowledge and partial hard-feature knowledge. They derive how hard-feature learning reaches a saturation level governed by the feature-strength-weighted balance of correct versus incorrect hard-only labels, and show that the student memorizes wrong labels via sample-specific noise while retaining hard-feature knowledge to achieve vanishing test error.
yTDcIt9mFZ.key_idea: Characterizes student hard-feature retention under weak supervision via a feature-strength-weighted balance of correct and noisy teacher labels coupled with benign sample-specific noise memorization.
yTDcIt9mFZ.evidence: Supported by gradient-descent learning-dynamics proofs for two-layer ReLU networks, synthetic experiments, and LLM sentiment classification and teacher-selection experiments.
yTDcIt9mFZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the natural problem formulation of partial teacher knowledge on hard features and the quantitative link showing why label accuracy weighted by hard-feature strength governs student generalization.
yTDcIt9mFZ.main_concern: Reviewers find the theoretical novelty incremental over prior two-layer ReLU benign-overfitting and easy/hard feature-learning analyses, noting that the teacher is modeled as random label noise on a linearly separable direction rather than a genuinely capacity-limited trained model.

xjrBG9BvCj.one_liner: Extracts proprietary RAG knowledge stealthily using semantic-network topic anchors and intent-constrained beam-search query rewriting.
xjrBG9BvCj.problem: Explicit knowledge extraction attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are easily caught by intent defenses, while implicit extraction attacks preserve stealth at the cost of low extraction coverage.
xjrBG9BvCj.method: SILK builds a semantic network of topic anchors, decomposes RAG outputs into atomic claims to measure fine-grained knowledge gain, and propagates observed knowledge density across the embedding neighborhood to select promising unexplored anchors. It then generates stealthy queries via constrained beam-search rewriting guided by a judge model and pruned by a shadow intent detector acting as a hard feasibility constraint.
xjrBG9BvCj.key_idea: Propagates atomic-claim knowledge gains across a semantic anchor graph to select targets and rewrites attack queries via constrained beam search filtered by a shadow intent detector.
xjrBG9BvCj.evidence: Evaluated across four datasets against six extraction baselines under multiple input/output defenses and RAG configurations.
xjrBG9BvCj.claimed_gains: SILK improves the knowledge leakage rate by 17% on average compared to the state-of-the-art implicit extraction method.
xjrBG9BvCj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining coverage-guided semantic anchor exploration with stealth-constrained query rewriting is a coherent approach to implicit RAG extraction, supported by broad experiments across datasets and defenses.
xjrBG9BvCj.main_concern: Reviewers point out that defining chunk leakage via ROUGE-L (>0.5) or semantic similarity (>0.65) without a non-RAG baseline control cannot distinguish proprietary retrieval extraction from the LLM's own pretrained parametric knowledge.

g1RBsPK44R.one_liner: Trains self-improving LLM agents across sequential task attempts using an RL reward derived from consecutive-episode verifiable task progress differences.
g1RBsPK44R.problem: Reinforcement learning methods for experiential learning in LLM agents rely on coarse binary outcome rewards that fail to directly credit whether distilled experience improved performance from one attempt to the next.
g1RBsPK44R.method: VEL formulates experiential learning across sequential episodes on the same task, where the agent distills experience from earlier attempts to guide subsequent attempts. It optimizes the agent with the Experience-Guided Advancement Reward (EGAR), defined as the difference in verifiable task progress between consecutive episodes.
g1RBsPK44R.key_idea: Rewards cross-episode experience distillation and reuse by computing the difference in environment-verifiable task progress scores between consecutive attempts on the same task.
g1RBsPK44R.evidence: Evaluated on four interactive agent benchmarks (including Sokoban) against RL baselines and experiential learning methods such as LaMer.
g1RBsPK44R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the cross-episode formulation and the idea of rewarding incremental verifiable progress differences between sequential attempts simple, intuitive, and well aligned with experiential learning.
g1RBsPK44R.main_concern: Reviewers note that EGAR requires environment-specific dense progress signals (degenerating to sparse {-1,0,1} differences under binary rewards), measures raw outcome differences rather than counterfactual experience credit, and omits a fair comparison against LaMer's reflection-only setting.

W8BViO3wZp.one_liner: Embeds training-free watermarks directly into 3D Gaussian Splatting DC colors via fruit-fly-connectome virtual photoreceptors and bounded QIM least squares.
W8BViO3wZp.problem: Existing 3D Gaussian Splatting watermarks rely on retraining, neural decoders, or multi-view rendering, so ownership evidence disappears if the auxiliary decoder or rendering pipeline is unavailable.
W8BViO3wZp.method: FlyMark defines fixed carrier directions using photoreceptor coordinates from a published fruit-fly connectome to read cone-wise apparent luminance along a scene-normalized orbit directly from stored 3DGS centers, colors, and opacities. It encodes message bits via keyed dithered quantization-index modulation (QIM) and solves a single sparse bounded least-squares problem to apply achromatic shifts to degree-zero (DC) colors under a hard per-channel RGB bound, leaving all geometry and higher-order spherical harmonics bit-identical.
W8BViO3wZp.key_idea: Projects stored 3DGS parameters onto fixed virtual photoreceptor cones from a fruit-fly connectome and embeds keyed QIM watermarks via bounded achromatic least-squares shifts on degree-zero colors.
W8BViO3wZp.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic and real 3DGS benchmarks including eight NeRF-Synthetic scenes and nine Mip-NeRF 360 scenes against baselines such as GuardSplat and 3D-GSW, plus a RandomCone-QIM control.
W8BViO3wZp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the training-free, decoder-free, parameter-domain watermark design that preserves geometry and higher-order appearance bit-identically and extracts bits via simple algebraic cone queries.
W8BViO3wZp.main_concern: Reviewers point out that a matched random-cone control performs almost as well (and slightly better under damage-matched comparisons), showing that the fruit-fly connectome itself adds little technical value over arbitrary deterministic directional lattices.

1G6idnFdJf.one_liner: Aligns phrase and image-region representations in text-to-image diffusion models within a shared hyperbolic space anchored to global scene context.
1G6idnFdJf.problem: Standard denoising objectives in text-to-image diffusion models provide weak supervision for binding specific prompt phrases to distinct local image regions without external teachers or bounding-box annotations.
1G6idnFdJf.method: Hierarchical Intermodal Projection (HIP) uses the diffusion generator's own joint attention and text representations during LoRA fine-tuning to align local image regions with prompt phrases while anchoring local features to their global semantic context. Both modalities are projected into a shared hyperbolic space to separate sibling concepts sharing the same global anchor, and the projection heads are discarded at inference.
1G6idnFdJf.key_idea: Projects self-extracted phrase and attention-region representations into a shared hyperbolic space with local cross-modal alignment and global scene-context anchoring during LoRA fine-tuning.
1G6idnFdJf.evidence: Evaluated on SD3.5-M and FLUX.1-dev backbones using GenEval, all six categories of T2I-CompBench, and COCO grounding evaluations.
1G6idnFdJf.claimed_gains: HIP improves GenEval macro accuracy by 14.48% on SD3.5-M and 8.24% on FLUX.1-dev relative to pretrained baselines, and achieves the highest scores across all six T2I-CompBench categories on both backbones.
1G6idnFdJf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that HIP leverages internal text and attention representations for phrase-region alignment without external teachers, region labels, or extra inference overhead.
1G6idnFdJf.main_concern: Reviewers note serious reproducibility inconsistencies disclosed in the code repository regarding mismatched configs, seed averaging, and missing main checkpoints, as well as insufficient isolation of hyperbolic geometry benefits over tuned Euclidean projections.

TZ1wo0IIKY.one_liner: Benchmarks 32 generalist graph anomaly detection methods across 22 graphs with organic and injected anomalies under unified transfer protocols.
TZ1wo0IIKY.problem: Generalist graph anomaly detection (GGAD) methods are evaluated on inconsistent datasets, anomaly types, and cross-graph transfer splits, hindering fair comparison.
TZ1wo0IIKY.method: GGADBench standardizes evaluation across 32 methods and 22 graph datasets encompassing both organic and synthetically injected anomalies. It assesses overall detection accuracy, cross-graph transferability, top-k anomaly retrieval, computational efficiency, and neighborhood deviation structure via an Anomaly Residual Polarity (ARP) statistic.
TZ1wo0IIKY.key_idea: Evaluates generalist graph anomaly detectors under a unified cross-graph transfer protocol across organic and injected anomalies while characterizing neighborhood deviation sign via Anomaly Residual Polarity.
TZ1wo0IIKY.evidence: Evaluated across 32 methods on 22 graph datasets (including Reddit, Tolokers, Weibo, and Questions) covering effectiveness, source-to-target transfer, anomaly retrieval, and efficiency.
TZ1wo0IIKY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a unified benchmark covering 22 datasets and over 30 methods across organic and injected anomalies fills a timely gap and yields useful insights on feature alignment and retrieval metrics.
TZ1wo0IIKY.main_concern: Reviewers point out a major methodological flaw where hyperparameters were tuned on four target graphs (Reddit, Tolokers, Weibo, Questions) that are simultaneously reported as unseen test targets in the main evaluation.

RE0kbqoEz8.one_liner: Establishes dimension-independent neural approximation and sample-complexity bounds for score-based diffusion models in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
RE0kbqoEz8.problem: Existing statistical convergence guarantees for diffusion models are mostly restricted to finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces and suffer from the curse of dimensionality, failing to explain scalability to functional or ultra-high-dimensional data.
RE0kbqoEz8.method: The authors formulate infinite-dimensional diffusion processes in Hilbert spaces by expressing score functions via Radon-Nikodym density ratios relative to a Gaussian base measure rather than Lebesgue measure. Using an anisotropic gamma-smooth function space with coordinate-wise smoothness growth and a Gaussian CDF transformation, they derive polynomial-order, dimension-independent approximation and finite-sample estimation error bounds for ReLU network score estimators.
RE0kbqoEz8.key_idea: Reformulates infinite-dimensional scores via Radon-Nikodym derivatives against a Gaussian reference measure and applies a Gaussian CDF transform in anisotropic gamma-smooth spaces to bound ReLU score estimation error.
RE0kbqoEz8.evidence: Purely theoretical statistical analysis establishing approximation error and finite-sample distribution estimation error bounds in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
RE0kbqoEz8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that developing a dimension-independent statistical theory for infinite-dimensional functional diffusion models relative to a Gaussian reference measure is an important and well-formulated theoretical question.
RE0kbqoEz8.main_concern: Reviewers point out that Assumption 4.2 imposes a uniform two-sided L-infinity bound on the Gaussian density ratio—contradicting the claim of eliminating density lower-bound assumptions—and note the lack of concrete distribution examples or matching minimax lower bounds.

qjCpA6jyLC.one_liner: PISA selects attention blocks through a coarse-to-fine key pyramid using LogSumExp scores over bounded candidate sets.
qjCpA6jyLC.problem: Exhaustively scoring all query-block pairs leaves conventional block-sparse attention selection quadratic in sequence length.
qjCpA6jyLC.method: PISA pools keys into a hierarchy and repeatedly selects top candidates from coarse to fine using LogSumExp scoring. Fused Triton kernels combine routing and scoring without materializing a full query-key score matrix.
qjCpA6jyLC.key_idea: Prune candidate key blocks level by level in a hierarchy using LogSumExp scores before computing sparse attention.
qjCpA6jyLC.evidence: Language-modeling and commonsense evaluations accompany RULER retrieval tests and training and inference block-selection timing experiments.
qjCpA6jyLC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find hierarchical block selection sensible and its attention-mass-based scoring technically useful.
qjCpA6jyLC.main_concern: Reported efficiency measures exclude attention over selected blocks and therefore do not establish complete-layer or end-to-end speedups.

umAC1Bunja.one_liner: GEAT selects locally reconstructed terminal states by replay-relative geometric novelty and uses the same score to reward exploration.
umAC1Bunja.problem: GFlowNet exploration can repeatedly acquire experiences already available through replay instead of discovering diverse high-reward objects.
umAC1Bunja.method: Novelty-aware termination generates candidates by local backtracking and reconstruction, selecting one for task-reward evaluation. An entropy-derived geometric novelty score measures candidate similarity to replay reference states and guides both exploration rewards and terminal selection.
umAC1Bunja.key_idea: Rank reconstructed terminal candidates by their first-order effect on geometry-aware replay entropy and evaluate only the most novel candidate.
umAC1Bunja.evidence: Benchmarks evaluate high-reward mode discovery, mode coverage, reward quality, and distributional accuracy, with component ablations described in reviews.
umAC1Bunja.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find exploration coverage important and the proposed combination clearly motivated with encouraging mode-discovery results.
umAC1Bunja.main_concern: The method mainly combines established GFlowNet exploration, replay, and local-search components without clearly establishing a distinct methodological advance.

G6Jms5aJl7.one_liner: MetaST predicts receiver-specific reconstruction value to allocate a shared transmission budget between pixel anchors and structural metadata.
G6Jms5aJl7.problem: Generative space-time super-resolution cannot reliably recover source-specific structure that was never transmitted.
G6Jms5aJl7.method: A sender learns metadata values from offline responses of a fixed receiver and predicts them from source and encoder statistics. Budgeted allocation lets pixel anchors and structural metadata compete for the same transmitted bytes without sender-side reconstruction.
G6Jms5aJl7.key_idea: Learn the receiver's reconstruction benefit for candidate transmitted representations and allocate bytes by predicted value.
G6Jms5aJl7.evidence: HC-Meta tests structural metadata and learned allocation, with additional H.264/H.266 and general-video experiments examining coding efficiency.
G6Jms5aJl7.claimed_gains: MetaST improves Average PSNR by 3.0 dB over the strongest pixel-only baseline at the lossless-anchor reference budget, recovers 79.4% of oracle allocation gain, and reduces regret by 33% relative to a rate-only predictor.
G6Jms5aJl7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value explicit shared-budget accounting for pixels and metadata and separate evaluation of structural information and allocation.
G6Jms5aJl7.main_concern: The headline structural-metadata gain does not establish the incremental value or generalizability of the learned allocation predictor.

CYaKCtbwGB.one_liner: Task-vector-guided projection and affine batch-normalization merging combine subject-specific EEG models without accessing recordings.
CYaKCtbwGB.problem: Conflicting subject updates and normalization states can erase accumulated EEG knowledge, while replay requires retaining sensitive recordings.
CYaKCtbwGB.method: RPT scales layer targets using task-vector agreement and selects incoming contributions through a closed-form history-weighted projection that preserves historical relative weights. AM-BN jointly merges the inference transformations defined by batch-normalization statistics and affine parameters.
CYaKCtbwGB.key_idea: Project incoming task vectors against history-weighted targets and merge batch-normalization affine maps rather than treating their parameters independently.
CYaKCtbwGB.evidence: Experiments across three EEG tasks compare continual merging methods and examine aggregate backward transfer and component ablations.
CYaKCtbwGB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find data-free continual EEG merging relevant and the treatment of conflicting updates and normalization differences well motivated.
CYaKCtbwGB.main_concern: Each incoming subject still requires a checkpoint trained on substantial labeled EEG, limiting applicability when new users provide only unlabeled data.

5bESKei7JK.one_liner: Conditionally normalized residual flows couple probabilistic forecasts with multiple complementary deterministic predictors.
5bESKei7JK.problem: Single deterministic forecasters limit prediction diversity and cannot characterize multiple plausible futures under nonstationary uncertainty.
5bESKei7JK.method: DiverseFlow combines structurally aligned predictors with conditional residual flow matching around deterministic forecasts. It learns residual scales before fitting normalized distributions and uses flow-generated forecasts to diversify point predictions.
5bESKei7JK.key_idea: Learn conditional residual scales and flows, then feed complementary generated forecasts into the combination of deterministic predictive views.
5bESKei7JK.evidence: Forecasting benchmarks evaluate point accuracy and probabilistic quality, with matched scaling controls and multi-seed normalization ablations.
5bESKei7JK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize promising evidence for conditional scale normalization and for connecting uncertainty modeling to point-forecast improvement.
5bESKei7JK.main_concern: Missing closely related residual-generation and deterministic controls leave the distinct contribution beyond existing forecasting components unclear.

ajM84XEygi.one_liner: Physics-aware continuous light fields reconstruct dense virtual sensor readouts for sparse dark-matter detector measurements.
ajM84XEygi.problem: Sparse, irregular, and inactive photomultiplier coverage degrades interaction-position reconstruction, especially near the PandaX-4T detector wall.
ajM84XEygi.method: BambooSR learns an event-conditioned continuous light field using priors for direct propagation and boundary reflection. Integrating the field over finite sensor footprints produces denser virtual readouts, including responses at inactive sensors.
ajM84XEygi.key_idea: Reconstruct a physics-guided continuous light field and integrate it over sensor footprints to synthesize denser detector measurements.
ajM84XEygi.evidence: The benchmark contains 112,890 paired simulated readouts and 5,583 real PandaX-4T Run 2 wall events, with implicit-representation and geometric baselines.
ajM84XEygi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of the detector-specific super-resolution task and its paired simulation benchmark with real-event evaluation.
ajM84XEygi.main_concern: Missing direct learned readout or position-reconstruction baselines leave the practical advantage of the two-stage super-resolution pipeline uncertain.

VB0Zsq3nYU.one_liner: Local query clustering and inclusion-weighted block sampling approximate dense video attention with fine-grained GPU block gathering.
VB0Zsq3nYU.problem: Aggressive block-sparse video attention loses fidelity through coarse importance estimates, discarded softmax contributions, and tile-level selection.
VB0Zsq3nYU.method: AB-Attention clusters queries within each block to estimate importance, then samples blocks and reweights them by inverse inclusion probability. Its kernel gathers small KV blocks into full tensor-core tiles without permuting tokens or adding training.
VB0Zsq3nYU.key_idea: Estimate block importance from local query clusters and inverse-weight sampled block contributions while packing fine-grained selections into tensor-core tiles.
VB0Zsq3nYU.evidence: Experiments on Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo include fixed-budget component ablations and attention recall and error analyses.
VB0Zsq3nYU.claimed_gains: AB-Attention skips 89--92% of attention while baselines compute 1.8--3.6× as much, and reports PSNR improvements of up to 4.4 dB.
VB0Zsq3nYU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the component-level design and ablations connecting attention approximation choices to execution constraints.
VB0Zsq3nYU.main_concern: Single operating-point comparisons and missing correction-based alternatives do not establish the quality-speed advantage under matched conditions.

qSAFcuWbeQ.one_liner: Signed gradient projections from self-generated traces guide KV-cache reconstruction without changing quantization format or storage.
qSAFcuWbeQ.problem: Token-wise reconstruction errors can reinforce or cancel, so minimizing them individually does not control quantization-induced generation drift.
qSAFcuWbeQ.method: TraceKV generates and replays a BF16 continuation to obtain multi-step KL gradients with respect to cached values. It accumulates signed error projections to choose independent or residual-feedback reconstruction per token, then selects candidate caches through replay.
qSAFcuWbeQ.key_idea: Choose token reconstructions using signed quantization-error projections onto trace KL gradients so positive and negative trajectory effects can cancel.
qSAFcuWbeQ.evidence: Experiments span four quantization representations, signed-versus-magnitude ablations, and free-running generation, with PatternKV and OSCAR gains persisting beyond the selection window.
qSAFcuWbeQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value improving generation fidelity through reconstruction choices at an unchanged persistent cache budget and find signed-error ablations supportive.
qSAFcuWbeQ.main_concern: BF16 tracing, gradient computation, cache construction, and replay overhead lack latency and peak-memory measurements.

DTjGV8TvzZ.one_liner: Matched executions compare unilateral and joint prompt repairs to co-adapt runtime context edits for frozen agents.
DTjGV8TvzZ.problem: Runtime instruction edits that help individually can interfere when combined because they change each other's interpretation or execution.
DTjGV8TvzZ.method: MICA uses matched executions to propose composition-mismatch hypotheses and minimal template repairs, then compares original, unilateral, and joint revisions at fixed edit structure. Competing structures receive equal adaptation allowances before execution-based selection, frozen screening, and independent deployment confirmation.
DTjGV8TvzZ.key_idea: Measure interactions through original, unilateral, and joint template revisions, then select edit structures after equal-budget co-adaptation.
DTjGV8TvzZ.evidence: Evaluation spans five environments with GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, common-budget Telecom and AppWorld Normal comparisons, and 20-run controlled mechanism studies.
DTjGV8TvzZ.claimed_gains: MICA reports macro-average scores of 80.90% with GPT-5.5 and 76.80% with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, exceeding their strongest baselines by 4.82 and 1.72 percentage points, respectively; common-budget gains over the strongest search baseline are 3.25 percentage points on Telecom and 4.23 percentage points on AppWorld Normal.
DTjGV8TvzZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate controlled intervention studies and separation of adaptation, screening, and deployment confirmation.
DTjGV8TvzZ.main_concern: Main benchmark comparisons use a single optimization seed, so repeated mechanism studies do not establish the stability of gains over strong baselines.

Y87dAq2dmj.one_liner: Opponent-type-indexed memories and randomized utility estimates adapt LLM strategies through game experience.
Y87dAq2dmj.problem: Opponent uncertainty, naive similarity retrieval, and outcome-only feedback make strategic memories difficult to retrieve and evaluate.
Y87dAq2dmj.method: OppoMem associates opponent types with response strategies and uses online opponent modeling to retrieve relevant memories. Randomized memory activation estimates individual utility and guides retention, revision, and removal.
Y87dAq2dmj.key_idea: Index strategies by opponent type and estimate each memory's utility through randomized activation before revising the memory store.
Y87dAq2dmj.evidence: Strategic-game experiments compare six baselines across two backbones and include a limited cross-game transfer study.
Y87dAq2dmj.claimed_gains: The abstract reports an average relative performance improvement around 30%.
